391 392 ### Deploy a Bundle 393 394 For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can only designate **one bundle at a time** as deployed for each environment. 395 396 1. Go to a project’s overview page. 397 2. Click the name of the environment you want to deploy to. For example: **production**. 398 3. Under the heading **Bundles**, click the **Deploy** button next to the bundle you want to deploy. 399 4. Click **Confirm Deploy**. 400 5. Wait until the deployment is complete. 401 402 When the deployment has successfully completed, the bundle appears underneath the heading **Deployed Bundle**. (For your first deployment to a new environment, the process can take up to an hour to complete.) 403 404 ### Delete a Bundle 405 406 For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can delete only non-deployed bundles form a project. 407 408 1. In the project’s overview page, click an environment. 409 2. Select one or more bundles that aren't currently deployed. 410 3. Click **Delete**. 411 4. When asked to confirm, click **Delete**. 412 5. Wait until the deletion is completed. 413 414 Deletions are handled asynchronously and can take time to process. 415 416 ### Edit Environment Settings 417 418 The Environment Settings page is where you can do many administration tasks in one place, including: 419 420 - Rename an environment or environment ID. 421 - Change the deployment region. 422 - Enable or disable server-side cookies. New projects have Server-Side Cookie Access enabled by default. Existing projects continue to have server-side cookies turned off by default. See [Personalize with Cookies](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/personalize-with-cookies.html). 423 - Enable or disable [Source Maps](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/debugging.html#source-maps). 424 - Allow traffic with specific IP addresses or a trusted access control header to access an environment. See [Access Control Headers](#access-control-headers). 425 - Configure proxies for an environment. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html) for more information. 426 - Control whether proxied requests forward the shopper's original user agent or replace it with the Amazon CloudFront infrastructure user agent. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html#request-modifications). 427 - Mark an environment as production. 428 - Add, edit, or remove site IDs associated with an environment. 429 - Add or edit an environment’s connection to a B2C Commerce instance. 430 - Delete an environment. 431 432 To access the Environment Settings page: 433 434 1. Go to a project’s Overview page 435 2. Click the name of the environment whose settings you want to edit. 436 3. Click **Environment Settings** from the left navigation. 437 438 To make edits, click the **Edit** button next to either the **General** settings or the **Advanced** settings. After making your edits, click **Update** to save your changes or click **Cancel** to discard your changes. 439 440 ### Server-Side Rendering Architecture 441 442 Managed Runtime supports two processor architectures for Server-Side Rendering (SSR): ARM and x86. The architecture determines the underlying compute infrastructure used to render your storefront. 443 444 #### ARM Architecture (Default for New Projects) 445 446 ARM architecture is the default for all new projects created in Managed Runtime. ARM processors offer several advantages. 447 448 - **Enhanced Performance**: ARM architecture provides efficient processing capabilities optimized for modern web workloads. 449 - **Modern Infrastructure**: Built on the latest cloud computing technologies. 450 451 **Who Can Use It**: All new Managed Runtime projects automatically use ARM architecture. 452 453 #### x86 Architecture (Scheduled for Retirement) 454 455 :::warning 456 The x86 architecture is retiring on **January 31, 2027**. After that date, environments running on x86 can't be deployed. Environments aren't deleted and continue to respond to requests. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. 457 ::: 458 459 The x86 architecture is available for existing customers until its retirement on January 31, 2027. 460 461 **Who**: Existing customers with projects created before ARM architecture was introduced can continue using x86 until January 31, 2027. 462 463 #### Choosing an Architecture 464 465 - **New Projects**: ARM architecture is automatically selected and is the recommended choice for all new projects. 466 - **Existing projects**: x86 architecture is retiring on January 31, 2027. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. Admins can switch existing environments to ARM at any time in Runtime Admin under environment settings. Most projects require no code changes. If your project uses architecture-specific native modules, test in a non-production environment before switching production. 467 468 #### Project-Level Default Architecture 469 470 You can set a default architecture at the project level that automatically applies to all new environments created within that project. This setting streamlines environment creation by eliminating the need to select an architecture for each new environment. 471 472 How to Set Project-Level Default: 473 474 1. Go to a project's Overview page. 475 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 476 3. Under **Environment Defaults** and **Server Architecture**, select either **ARM** or **x86**. 477 4. Click **Update**. 478 479 All new environments created in the project automatically use the selected default architecture. Existing environments aren't affected by changes to the project-level default. 480 481 ### Clear an Environment's CDN Cache 482 483 You can clear some or all of an environment's cached content in the content delivery network (CDN). Clearing the CDN cache helps to ensure that shoppers see the most recent and accurate version of content on your site. 484 485 Use the [projects_target_invalidation_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_invalidation_create) API to clear all cached content, specific URLs, or directories. 486 487 It's not possible to clear the CDN cache in Runtime Admin. However, when you redeploy a bundle, that clears all cached content for the associated environment. 488 489 :::note 490 Invalidation of the CDN cache temporarily results in slower performance for the first shoppers accessing the site after the invalidation. 491 ::: 492 493 ## Environment Variables 494 495 See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.html). 496 497 ## Access Control Headers 498 499 Access control headers allow you to restrict access to an environment so that only trusted traffic coming from your content delivery network (CDN) or development team is allowed. Restricting access is important to ensure that bots don't go around your CDN perimeter security settings and to ensure that search crawlers don’t index content from the wrong domain or environment. 500 501 If Allowed IP addresses are also set, requests with either a valid IP address or an access control header are allowed through. 502 503 ### Usage 504 505 Set access control headers by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 506 507 Incoming requests are allowed only if an `x-sfdc-access-control` request header is present with a valid value. 508 509 ### Constraints 510 511 A header value is made up of your chosen set of characters. Each header value: 512 513 - Must be at least 9 characters long 514 - Can contain up to 128 characters 515 - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and `-` and `_` characters 516 517 Access control headers are not available to code running in a Managed Runtime environment. 518 519 ### Rotate Access Control Headers 520 521 You’re responsible for ensuring that the access control header value is securely stored and shared only with trusted individuals. We strongly recommend rotating the access control header on a regular basis. 522 523 To rotate an access control header: 524 525 - Add an access control header value to the Managed Runtime environment by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 526 - Wait for the Environment redeploy to complete successfully. Verify requests to the environment with the new header value succeed with a command such as: 527 528 ```bash 529 curl https://myproject-mytarget.mobify-storefront.com/ -H "x-sfdc-access-control: 123456789" -o /dev/null 530 ``` 531 532 - Update your CDN or browser to send the `x-sfdc-access-control` request header with the updated value. 533 - Test that traffic is being allowed through as expected. 534 - Remove the original access control header value by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 535 536 **See Also** 537 538 - [Configure Your Environment](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#5-configure-your-environment) 539 540 ## Redirects 541 542 A redirect allows you to forward a request from the requested URL to a different URL. Redirects can help avoid disruptions to the user experience caused by changes to your storefront. For example, consider a seasonal campaign page for spring. When the spring campaign ends and is replaced with a summer campaign, you can redirect from the spring URL to the summer URL. 543 544 Redirects is a powerful feature that can have significant security consequences on your storefront, including redirecting to malicious URLs or assets. Please be careful when assigning roles to your users that give them Redirect access. 545 546 ### Create a Redirect 547 548 :::tip 549 Before creating a redirect in a production environment, we recommend that you create it in a staging environment first. 550 ::: 551 552 You can also create one or more redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_create](/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_create) API endpoint. 553 554 To create a redirect using Runtime Admin: 555 556 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 557 2. Click the name of the environment where you want to create the redirect. 558 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 559 4. Click **Create Redirect**. 560 5. In the **Redirect From** field, enter a relative URL path. For example, to redirect visitors from the URL `www.example.com/winter`, enter `/winter`. 561 6. In the **Redirect To** field, enter a relative URL path. 562 7. If needed, enable forwarding of query parameters and the wildcard path. (More information on forwarding settings in a moment.) 563 8. From the **Redirect Type** dropdown menu, select a redirect type based on the HTTP status code. (More information on status codes in a moment.) 564 9. Click **Create Redirect**. 565 566 Let’s look at the options for creating a redirect in more detail. 567 568 #### Paths 569 570 The value that you enter in the **Redirect From** field must always be a *relative* path. The **Redirect To** field can be either a relative path or a full URL. For example, imagine that we want to redirect visitors from `www.example.com/spring` to `www.example.com/summer`. The **Redirect From** field must be `/spring`. The **Redirect To** field can be either `/summer` or `www.example.com/summer`. 571 572 #### Wildcards 573 574 You can add an asterisk character (`*`) to the end of the **Redirect From** URL to indicate a wildcard. A wildcard matches any (0 or more) characters in the URL. For example, a redirect from `/a/*` would match `/a/`, `/a/b`, and `/a/b/c`. 575 576 A wildcard character can only be used at the end of the **Redirect From** URL. 577 578 Standard redirects are processed first by Managed Runtime, followed by redirects with wildcards. 579 580 #### HTTP Status Codes 581 582 Most redirects use the Permanent 301 status code, but you can also select Temporary 302. If you’re unsure which HTTP status code to use, consult this [status code explainer](https://moz.com/learn/seo/redirection) from MOZ.com. 583 584 #### Forwarding Query Parameters 585 586 Some requests contain query string parameters that you also want to include in the redirected request. For example, the relative path `/spring-landing-page` can be appended with a query string for analytics tracking, such as `/spring-landing-page?gclid=123`. 587 588 To enable query parameter forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Query Parameters**. Otherwise, query string parameters from the source URL aren’t included in the redirect URL. 589 590 What happens when both the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** URLs both have query strings and forwarding is enabled? In this case, the redirect URL includes a combination of the two query strings. The query parameters from the **Redirect To** URL are appended to the query string in the request. For example, imagine your application receives a request for the relative path `/spring?year=2019`. If you’ve chosen to redirect `/spring` to `/summer?year=2020`, the redirect URL is `/summer?year=2019&year=2020` when forwarding is enabled. 591 592 #### Forwarding Wildcard Path 593 594 You can automatically include any path that comes after the wildcard portion of the **Redirect From** URL in the **Redirect To** URL. For example: if `/a/*` matches `/a/b/c` in the **Redirect From** URL, and the **Redirect To** URL is `/z/`, the redirect URL is `/z/b/c`. 595 596 To enable wildcard path forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Wildcard Path**. 597 598 ### Clone Redirects 599 600 :::tip 601 We recommend that you always create redirects in a staging environment and clone them into production after testing them. 602 ::: 603 604 You can copy all the redirects from one environment to another using the clone redirects feature. 605 606 You can also clone redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_clone_create ](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_clone_create) API endpoint. 607 608 To clone redirects using Runtime Admin: 609 610 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 611 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirects that you want to clone. 612 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 613 4. Click **Clone Redirects**. The **Clone Redirects** form appears. The current environment is listed under **From Environment** (the source). 614 5. Under **To Environment**, select the environment that you want to clone the redirects into (the destination). 615 6. Click **Clone n Redirects**. (Where n is the number of redirects to be cloned.) 616 617 :::warning 618 When you clone redirects, you’re replacing *all* the redirects in the destination environment with *all* the redirects from the source environment. 619 ::: 620 621 ### Edit a Redirect 622 623 You can also edit a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_partial_update) API endpoint. 624 625 To edit the settings for an existing redirect using Runtime Admin: 626 627 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 628 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to edit. 629 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 630 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 631 5. Click **Edit**. 632 6. Update the settings. 633 7. Click **Update Redirect**. 634 635 ### Delete a Redirect 636 637 You can also delete a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_destroy](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_destroy) API endpoint. 638 639 To delete a redirect using Runtime Admin: 640 641 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 642 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to delete. 643 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 644 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 645 5. Click **Delete**. 646 6. Click **Yes, Delete Redirect**. 647 648 ### Troubleshooting Redirects 649 650 If a redirect isn’t working as expected, try these troubleshooting steps: 651 652 - [Clear your browser cache](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop\&hl=en) because redirects are cached. 653 - Verify that you’re viewing the settings for the correct environment. 654 - Edit the redirect and verify that the correct values are entered in the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** fields. 655 656 ### Technical Limitations with Redirects 657 658 Redirects have the following technical limitations: 659 660 - Each environment can have a maximum of 10,000 redirects. 661 - Each environment has its own set of redirects. It is your responsibility to keep them in sync using cloning. 662 - The redirects feature supports simple redirects from one path to another. For complex redirects with conditionals use Express.js' [redirects support](http://expressjs.com/en/api.html#res.redirect) in `ssr.js`. 663 - Redirects created with the Runtime Admin tool or the Managed Runtime API are not run on local development environments. 664 - Redirects are not triggered by page transitions in the PWA Kit application; they can only be triggered by an HTTP request. 665 - To load a redirect in the context of a storefront, use the managed endpoint `/mobify/redirect/$path`. 666 667 ## Users 668 669 Here’s how to manage your users. 670 671 ### Add a User 672 673 To add a user to a project: 674 675 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 676 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 677 3. Click **New User**. 678 4. Enter the user’s email address. (Make sure that the user is part of your organization and has either one of the following roles in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.) 679 5. Select a role. 680 6. Click **Add User**. 681 682 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-2.png) 683 684 ### Change a User’s Role 685 686 To change a user’s role: 687 688 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 689 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 690 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 691 4. Click **Edit**. 692 5. Select a role. 693 6. Click the popup menu that appears. 694 7. Select a new role. 695 8. Click **Save**. 696 697 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-3.png) 698 699 For a list of user abilities associated with each role, see the [Managed Runtime Overview](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/mrt-overview.html). 700 701 ### Remove a User 702 703 To remove a user from a project: 704 705 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 706 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 707 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 708 4. Click **Remove**. 709 5. Click **Yes, Remove User**. 710 711 ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-4.png) 712

# Managed Runtime Administration Managed Runtime makes it easy to manage your organizations, projects, environments, and bundles associated with your PWA Kit storefront. This guide describes the growing list of administration tasks that are possible in the web-based [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/) tool. All of the administration tasks described in this guide, and many more, can also be done using the [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary). :::important Before you continue, make sure that you have access to Managed Runtime and [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). To provision Managed Runtime, contact your Success Manager. For Runtime Admin, contact your B2C Commerce administrator and ask them to add either one of the following roles to your account using Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**. ::: ## Organization Organization-level administration allows you to manage users and certificates across all projects within your organization. These tasks are typically performed by organization admins or users with specific organizational permissions. ### Managing Organization Users Organization admins can manage user access and permissions at the organization level, which affects user access across all projects within the organization. #### Add Organization Users To add a user at the organization level: 1. Log in to [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com/). 2. Find the users in your organization that need access. 3. Add the **Managed Runtime Admin** or **Managed Runtime User** role and save. Users should now be able to log into [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/) for your organization. :::note Users added at the organization level still need to be assigned specific project roles to access individual projects. ::: #### Edit Organization User Permissions To modify a user's organization-level permissions: 1. Navigate to **Organiation Users**. 2. Click **Edit** next to the user's name. 3. Modify the permissions as needed. - **Certificates**: Allows the user to view, request, manage, and renew TLS certificates. - **View All Projects**: Allows read-only access to all projects within the organization. 4. Click **Save**. #### Remove Organization Users To remove a user from the organization: 1. Log in to [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com/). 2. Find the users in your organization that need access. 3. Remove the **Managed Runtime Admin** or **Managed Runtime User** role and save. :::warning Removing a user from Managed Runtime revokes their access to all projects within the organization. ::: ### Certificate Management Organization admins and users with the **Manage Certificates** permission can manage TLS certificates for environments using the Managed Runtime CDN. #### Prerequisites for Certificate Management - Organization Admin role OR **Manage Certificates** permission. - Access to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). #### Request a Certificate To request a new TLS certificate: 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). 2. Navigate to **Certificates** for an organization. 3. Click **Request Certificate**. 4. Enter the domains you want to include in the certificate. - Fully qualified domains (e.g., `www.example.com`, `staging.example.com`) - Wildcard domains (e.g., `*.example.com`) 5. Click **Send Request**. The certificate request will be processed, and you'll receive domain validation instructions. #### Domain Validation After requesting a certificate, you must validate domain ownership. 1. Navigate to **Certificate** and click on the pending certificate. 2. Copy the CNAME records provided for domain validation. 3. Add these CNAME records to your DNS configuration. 4. Validation records must be created within **72 hours** of receiving the validation details. 5. After the DNS records are in place, the certificate request will be validated and available to use with any environments within the organization. Example validation record: ``` _xyz.example.com CNAME _abc.acm-validations.aws ``` #### Monitor Certificate Status To view the status of your certificates: 1. Navigate to **Certificates**. 2. View the certificate list with validation status indicators. - **In Progress**: Awaiting domain validation. - **Validation Completed**: Certificate is validated and ready for use. - **Failed**: Validation failed because the provided CNAME record wasn't added on time. #### Certificate Renewal Managed Runtime automatically renews certificates as long as: - The domain validation CNAME records remain in place. - The certificate is actively used by at least one environment. #### Associate Certificates with Environments To use a certificate with an environment: 1. Go to the project's Overview page. 2. Click the environment name. 3. Click **Environment Settings**. 4. Under **Advanced** settings, click **Edit**. 5. Select the appropriate certificate from the **Certificate** dropdown. 6. For wildcard certificates, provide a valid subdomain. 7. Click **Update**. 8. Follow the instructions in [Launching Your Storefront](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#6-perform-the-cutover). :::important - Users must have the **Project Admin** or **Project Developer** role and the organization **View** or **Manage** certificate permission to change certificates. - Certificates can only be used with environments in the same organization. - Changes to certificate associations require environment redeployment. ::: #### Certificate Troubleshooting If you encounter issues with certificates: - **Domain Validation Fails**: Verify CNAME records are correctly configured and propagated with the validation window. ## Projects Projects help you manage multiple environments within an organization. Every PWA Kit project needs a corresponding project within Managed Runtime for deploying and hosting the storefront code on Salesforce’s public cloud infrastructure. :::note While this guide describes how to manage projects using the web-based Runtime Admin tool, you can use the B2C Commerce CLI to manage Managed Runtime (MRT) projects, environments, and deployments directly from your terminal. First, see [B2C CLI, MCP and Tooling SDK](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/b2c-developer-tooling.html) to install the tool and authenticate. Once configured, use the CLI to streamline MRT administration, for example: ```bash # List all Managed Runtime projects b2c mrt project list # Deploy a specific bundle to an environment b2c mrt bundle deploy --project --environment # Manage environments and environment variables b2c mrt env list --project b2c mrt env var --project --environment # Manage URL redirects for an environment b2c mrt env redirect --project --environment ``` For a complete list of Managed Runtime CLI commands, see [MRT Commands](https://salesforcecommercecloud.github.io/b2c-developer-tooling/cli/mrt.html). ::: ### Create a Project To create a project in Runtime Admin: 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com). 2. Click **New Project**. 3. Under **Add New Project Details**, enter a name for the project. 4. Under **Set Environment Defaults**, review the default settings that apply to new environments in the project. Server-Side Cookie Access is enabled by default for new projects, which lets your storefront access and manage cookies from server-side code. To turn it off, clear the setting. 5. Click **Create Project**. :::note When you first create a project, your site isn’t accessible on the web until after the necessary cloud infrastructure is deployed. This deployment process can take up to 40 minutes. ::: ### Find a Project in Runtime Admin The instructions for the rest of the administration tasks in this guide all assume that you’re starting from a project Overview page in Runtime Admin. To find an existing project and open its Overview page: 1. Log in to [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). 2. Select an organization from the organization menu (top left), if necessary. 3. Click the name of the project. (To see the project, you must be assigned one of the project roles described previously.) ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-1.png) To find a project quickly, use the project search box to filter across all the projects in your organization, not just the ones on the current page. You can also choose how many projects to show per page (20, 50, or 100). Your search term and page size are saved in the page URL, so you can bookmark or share a filtered view. To quickly switch between projects, use the project menu at the top of the page. ### View and Edit Project Settings The Project Settings page is where you can do the following tasks: - Look up the project ID and ensure that it matches a PWA Kit configuration. - Edit the project ID. - View and edit the project’s name and URL. - Set environment defaults, including the default server architecture and proxy user agent for new environments. - Delete the project. - Manage deployment notifications. (See next section.) To access the Project Settings page: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click Project Settings from the left navigation. To edit the settings, click **Edit**, make your edits, and click **Update**. To discard your edits, click **Cancel**. To delete a project, click **Delete**, enter the project name to confirm, and click **Yes, Delete**. To keep the project, click **No, Keep**. ## Deployment Notifications You can choose to be notified by email whenever any of the following deployment events happen: - Start Deployment - Successful Deployment - Failed Deployment ### Add a Notification To add a notification: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Click **Add Notification**. 4. Select one or more environments to be notified about. 5. Select one or more deployment events. 6. Enter email addresses for all notification recipients. 7. Click **Add Notification**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-5.png) ### Edit a Notification To edit a notification: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the notification. 4. Click **Edit**. 5. Change any of the notification settings. 6. Click **Update Notification**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-6.png) ### Remove a Notification To remove a notification: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the notification. 4. Click **Remove**. 5. Click **Yes, Remove**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-7.png) ## Environments Environments are used to separate your production storefront from other storefronts that are deployed for other purposes, such as development or testing. To learn more about environments and other related concepts, see the [Managed Runtime Overview](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/mrt-overview.html). ### Create an Environment To create an environment in Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **New Environment** 3. Enter a name for the environment. 4. Select a [region](#supported-regions) for deploying to Salesforce’s public cloud infrastructure. 5. If the environment is a production environment: - Mark it as production. If you have reached your limit of production environments, contact Support. For more information, see [Production Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/mrt-overview.html#production-environments). - Add one or more site IDs to associate with the environment. 6. Select a B2C Commerce instance to connect to the environment. 7. Click **Complete Setup**. :::note - The default region for new environments is US East (N. Virginia) because it’s located closest to on-demand sandboxes, which are commonly associated with development and testing environments. - If you previously created an environment, you can [Edit Environment Settings](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html?#edit-environment-settings) to connect it to a B2C Commerce instance and one or more site IDs. - There is no difference in the resources provided to a production or non-production environment. All environments automatically scale to handle traffic in the same way. For details, see [Production Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/mrt-overview.html#production-environments). ::: ### Supported Regions All supported regions have a paired backup region for failovers. You're responsible for ensuring that your application runs correctly in the selected primary and backup regions:
Primary Region Backup Region
us-east-1 - US East (N. Virginia) us-east-2 - US East (Ohio)
us-east-2 - US East (Ohio) us-east-1 - US East (N. Virginia)
us-west-1 - US West (N. California) us-west-2 - US West (Oregon)
us-west-2 - US West (Oregon) us-west-1 - US West (N. California)
ca-central-1 - Canada (Central) us-east-2 - US East (Ohio)
sa-east-1 - South America (São Paulo) us-east-1 - US East (Northern Virginia)
ap-south-1 - Asia Pacific (Mumbai) ap-south-2 - Asia Pacific (Hyderabad)
ap-south-2 - Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) ap-south-1 - Asia Pacific (Mumbai)
ap-southeast-1 - Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-northeast-2 - Asia Pacific (Seoul)
ap-southeast-2 - Asia Pacific (Sydney) ap-southeast-1 - Asia Pacific (Singapore)
ap-southeast-3 - Asia Pacific (Jakarta) ap-southeast-1 - Asia Pacific (Singapore)
ap-northeast-2 - Asia Pacific (Seoul) ap-southeast-1 - Asia Pacific (Singapore)
ap-northeast-1 - Asia Pacific (Tokyo) ap-northeast-3 - Asia Pacific (Osaka)
ap-northeast-3 - Asia Pacific (Osaka) ap-northeast-1 - Asia Pacific (Tokyo)
eu-west-1 - EU (Ireland) eu-west-3 - EU (Paris)
eu-west-2 - EU (London) eu-west-1 - EU (Ireland)
eu-west-3 - EU (Paris) eu-central-1 - EU (Frankfurt)
eu-central-1 - EU (Frankfurt) eu-west-3 - EU (Paris)
eu-central-2 - EU (Zurich) eu-central-1 - EU (Frankfurt)
eu-south-1 - EU (Milan) eu-central-1 - EU (Frankfurt)
me-central-1 - Middle East (United Arab Emirates) eu-west-2 - EU (London)
il-central-1 - Israel (Tel Aviv) eu-west-2 - EU (London)
### Deploy a Bundle For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can only designate **one bundle at a time** as deployed for each environment. 1. Go to a project’s overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment you want to deploy to. For example: **production**. 3. Under the heading **Bundles**, click the **Deploy** button next to the bundle you want to deploy. 4. Click **Confirm Deploy**. 5. Wait until the deployment is complete. When the deployment has successfully completed, the bundle appears underneath the heading **Deployed Bundle**. (For your first deployment to a new environment, the process can take up to an hour to complete.) ### Delete a Bundle For any site that uses PWA Kit and Managed Runtime, you can delete only non-deployed bundles form a project. 1. In the project’s overview page, click an environment. 2. Select one or more bundles that aren't currently deployed. 3. Click **Delete**. 4. When asked to confirm, click **Delete**. 5. Wait until the deletion is completed. Deletions are handled asynchronously and can take time to process. ### Edit Environment Settings The Environment Settings page is where you can do many administration tasks in one place, including: - Rename an environment or environment ID. - Change the deployment region. - Enable or disable server-side cookies. New projects have Server-Side Cookie Access enabled by default. Existing projects continue to have server-side cookies turned off by default. See [Personalize with Cookies](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/personalize-with-cookies.html). - Enable or disable [Source Maps](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/debugging.html#source-maps). - Allow traffic with specific IP addresses or a trusted access control header to access an environment. See [Access Control Headers](#access-control-headers). - Configure proxies for an environment. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html) for more information. - Control whether proxied requests forward the shopper's original user agent or replace it with the Amazon CloudFront infrastructure user agent. See [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html#request-modifications). - Mark an environment as production. - Add, edit, or remove site IDs associated with an environment. - Add or edit an environment’s connection to a B2C Commerce instance. - Delete an environment. To access the Environment Settings page: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page 2. Click the name of the environment whose settings you want to edit. 3. Click **Environment Settings** from the left navigation. To make edits, click the **Edit** button next to either the **General** settings or the **Advanced** settings. After making your edits, click **Update** to save your changes or click **Cancel** to discard your changes. ### Server-Side Rendering Architecture Managed Runtime supports two processor architectures for Server-Side Rendering (SSR): ARM and x86. The architecture determines the underlying compute infrastructure used to render your storefront. #### ARM Architecture (Default for New Projects) ARM architecture is the default for all new projects created in Managed Runtime. ARM processors offer several advantages. - **Enhanced Performance**: ARM architecture provides efficient processing capabilities optimized for modern web workloads. - **Modern Infrastructure**: Built on the latest cloud computing technologies. **Who Can Use It**: All new Managed Runtime projects automatically use ARM architecture. #### x86 Architecture (Scheduled for Retirement) :::warning The x86 architecture is retiring on **January 31, 2027**. After that date, environments running on x86 can't be deployed. Environments aren't deleted and continue to respond to requests. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. ::: The x86 architecture is available for existing customers until its retirement on January 31, 2027. **Who**: Existing customers with projects created before ARM architecture was introduced can continue using x86 until January 31, 2027. #### Choosing an Architecture - **New Projects**: ARM architecture is automatically selected and is the recommended choice for all new projects. - **Existing projects**: x86 architecture is retiring on January 31, 2027. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. Admins can switch existing environments to ARM at any time in Runtime Admin under environment settings. Most projects require no code changes. If your project uses architecture-specific native modules, test in a non-production environment before switching production. #### Project-Level Default Architecture You can set a default architecture at the project level that automatically applies to all new environments created within that project. This setting streamlines environment creation by eliminating the need to select an architecture for each new environment. How to Set Project-Level Default: 1. Go to a project's Overview page. 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 3. Under **Environment Defaults** and **Server Architecture**, select either **ARM** or **x86**. 4. Click **Update**. All new environments created in the project automatically use the selected default architecture. Existing environments aren't affected by changes to the project-level default. ### Clear an Environment's CDN Cache You can clear some or all of an environment's cached content in the content delivery network (CDN). Clearing the CDN cache helps to ensure that shoppers see the most recent and accurate version of content on your site. Use the [projects_target_invalidation_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_invalidation_create) API to clear all cached content, specific URLs, or directories. It's not possible to clear the CDN cache in Runtime Admin. However, when you redeploy a bundle, that clears all cached content for the associated environment. :::note Invalidation of the CDN cache temporarily results in slower performance for the first shoppers accessing the site after the invalidation. ::: ## Environment Variables See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.html). ## Access Control Headers Access control headers allow you to restrict access to an environment so that only trusted traffic coming from your content delivery network (CDN) or development team is allowed. Restricting access is important to ensure that bots don't go around your CDN perimeter security settings and to ensure that search crawlers don’t index content from the wrong domain or environment. If Allowed IP addresses are also set, requests with either a valid IP address or an access control header are allowed through. ### Usage Set access control headers by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. Incoming requests are allowed only if an `x-sfdc-access-control` request header is present with a valid value. ### Constraints A header value is made up of your chosen set of characters. Each header value: - Must be at least 9 characters long - Can contain up to 128 characters - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and `-` and `_` characters Access control headers are not available to code running in a Managed Runtime environment. ### Rotate Access Control Headers You’re responsible for ensuring that the access control header value is securely stored and shared only with trusted individuals. We strongly recommend rotating the access control header on a regular basis. To rotate an access control header: - Add an access control header value to the Managed Runtime environment by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. - Wait for the Environment redeploy to complete successfully. Verify requests to the environment with the new header value succeed with a command such as: ```bash curl https://myproject-mytarget.mobify-storefront.com/ -H "x-sfdc-access-control: 123456789" -o /dev/null ``` - Update your CDN or browser to send the `x-sfdc-access-control` request header with the updated value. - Test that traffic is being allowed through as expected. - Remove the original access control header value by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. **See Also** - [Configure Your Environment](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#5-configure-your-environment) ## Redirects A redirect allows you to forward a request from the requested URL to a different URL. Redirects can help avoid disruptions to the user experience caused by changes to your storefront. For example, consider a seasonal campaign page for spring. When the spring campaign ends and is replaced with a summer campaign, you can redirect from the spring URL to the summer URL. Redirects is a powerful feature that can have significant security consequences on your storefront, including redirecting to malicious URLs or assets. Please be careful when assigning roles to your users that give them Redirect access. ### Create a Redirect :::tip Before creating a redirect in a production environment, we recommend that you create it in a staging environment first. ::: You can also create one or more redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_create](/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_create) API endpoint. To create a redirect using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment where you want to create the redirect. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click **Create Redirect**. 5. In the **Redirect From** field, enter a relative URL path. For example, to redirect visitors from the URL `www.example.com/winter`, enter `/winter`. 6. In the **Redirect To** field, enter a relative URL path. 7. If needed, enable forwarding of query parameters and the wildcard path. (More information on forwarding settings in a moment.) 8. From the **Redirect Type** dropdown menu, select a redirect type based on the HTTP status code. (More information on status codes in a moment.) 9. Click **Create Redirect**. Let’s look at the options for creating a redirect in more detail. #### Paths The value that you enter in the **Redirect From** field must always be a *relative* path. The **Redirect To** field can be either a relative path or a full URL. For example, imagine that we want to redirect visitors from `www.example.com/spring` to `www.example.com/summer`. The **Redirect From** field must be `/spring`. The **Redirect To** field can be either `/summer` or `www.example.com/summer`. #### Wildcards You can add an asterisk character (`*`) to the end of the **Redirect From** URL to indicate a wildcard. A wildcard matches any (0 or more) characters in the URL. For example, a redirect from `/a/*` would match `/a/`, `/a/b`, and `/a/b/c`. A wildcard character can only be used at the end of the **Redirect From** URL. Standard redirects are processed first by Managed Runtime, followed by redirects with wildcards. #### HTTP Status Codes Most redirects use the Permanent 301 status code, but you can also select Temporary 302. If you’re unsure which HTTP status code to use, consult this [status code explainer](https://moz.com/learn/seo/redirection) from MOZ.com. #### Forwarding Query Parameters Some requests contain query string parameters that you also want to include in the redirected request. For example, the relative path `/spring-landing-page` can be appended with a query string for analytics tracking, such as `/spring-landing-page?gclid=123`. To enable query parameter forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Query Parameters**. Otherwise, query string parameters from the source URL aren’t included in the redirect URL. What happens when both the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** URLs both have query strings and forwarding is enabled? In this case, the redirect URL includes a combination of the two query strings. The query parameters from the **Redirect To** URL are appended to the query string in the request. For example, imagine your application receives a request for the relative path `/spring?year=2019`. If you’ve chosen to redirect `/spring` to `/summer?year=2020`, the redirect URL is `/summer?year=2019&year=2020` when forwarding is enabled. #### Forwarding Wildcard Path You can automatically include any path that comes after the wildcard portion of the **Redirect From** URL in the **Redirect To** URL. For example: if `/a/*` matches `/a/b/c` in the **Redirect From** URL, and the **Redirect To** URL is `/z/`, the redirect URL is `/z/b/c`. To enable wildcard path forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Wildcard Path**. ### Clone Redirects :::tip We recommend that you always create redirects in a staging environment and clone them into production after testing them. ::: You can copy all the redirects from one environment to another using the clone redirects feature. You can also clone redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_clone_create ](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_clone_create) API endpoint. To clone redirects using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirects that you want to clone. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click **Clone Redirects**. The **Clone Redirects** form appears. The current environment is listed under **From Environment** (the source). 5. Under **To Environment**, select the environment that you want to clone the redirects into (the destination). 6. Click **Clone n Redirects**. (Where n is the number of redirects to be cloned.) :::warning When you clone redirects, you’re replacing *all* the redirects in the destination environment with *all* the redirects from the source environment. ::: ### Edit a Redirect You can also edit a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_partial_update) API endpoint. To edit the settings for an existing redirect using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to edit. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 5. Click **Edit**. 6. Update the settings. 7. Click **Update Redirect**. ### Delete a Redirect You can also delete a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_destroy](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_destroy) API endpoint. To delete a redirect using Runtime Admin: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to delete. 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 5. Click **Delete**. 6. Click **Yes, Delete Redirect**. ### Troubleshooting Redirects If a redirect isn’t working as expected, try these troubleshooting steps: - [Clear your browser cache](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop\&hl=en) because redirects are cached. - Verify that you’re viewing the settings for the correct environment. - Edit the redirect and verify that the correct values are entered in the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** fields. ### Technical Limitations with Redirects Redirects have the following technical limitations: - Each environment can have a maximum of 10,000 redirects. - Each environment has its own set of redirects. It is your responsibility to keep them in sync using cloning. - The redirects feature supports simple redirects from one path to another. For complex redirects with conditionals use Express.js' [redirects support](http://expressjs.com/en/api.html#res.redirect) in `ssr.js`. - Redirects created with the Runtime Admin tool or the Managed Runtime API are not run on local development environments. - Redirects are not triggered by page transitions in the PWA Kit application; they can only be triggered by an HTTP request. - To load a redirect in the context of a storefront, use the managed endpoint `/mobify/redirect/$path`. ## Users Here’s how to manage your users. ### Add a User To add a user to a project: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 3. Click **New User**. 4. Enter the user’s email address. (Make sure that the user is part of your organization and has either one of the following roles in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.) 5. Select a role. 6. Click **Add User**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-2.png) ### Change a User’s Role To change a user’s role: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 4. Click **Edit**. 5. Select a role. 6. Click the popup menu that appears. 7. Select a new role. 8. Click **Save**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-3.png) For a list of user abilities associated with each role, see the [Managed Runtime Overview](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/mrt-overview.html). ### Remove a User To remove a user from a project: 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 2. Click **Users & Permissions** from the left navigation. 3. Click the **...** button next to the user’s name. 4. Click **Remove**. 5. Click **Yes, Remove User**. ![Associated screenshot](https://a.sfdcstatic.com/developer-website/sfdocs/commerce-cloud/media/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/runtime-admin-4.png)

I've found the official MRT documentation, which confirms that Managed Runtime is indeed the infrastructure layer for deploying, hosting, and monitoring PWA Kit storefronts—so my earlier characterization was on the right track. More importantly, there's an actual Managed Runtime Admin API that I need to examine more closely.

This API handles deployment and administration functions like managing environments, bundles, deployments, redirects, proxies, access control headers, CDN cache invalidation, environment variables, certificates, and user management. This is a genuine, distinct API called the Managed Runtime API, which creates an interesting tension with my audit's central argument that "MRT is not an API; the API is SCAPI."

The ticket asks me to document MRT API capabilities, and now I'm seeing there are two legitimate interpretations: the literal Managed Runtime Admin API (the deployment/administration REST interface) versus the broader commerce data APIs. I need to clarify which one the ticket is actually asking for.

Looking at the ticket's stated objective and background, the intent is clearly about product, pricing, and category data consumption before MuleSoft is ready — that's the SCAPI path through the MRT proxy. But my deliverable's flat statement that "MRT is not an API" is technically inaccurate because the Managed Runtime API does exist as an administration API. I should reframe this to acknowledge both: MRT has an administration/deployment API, but the data serving product and pricing information comes through SCAPI via the MRT proxy layer.

The audit should flag that my doc needs to explicitly scope out the Managed Runtime API with a clear reason — it's platform administration, not data consumption — rather than deny its existence. This makes the doc more precise and authoritative to readers who know the real MRT API.

Now I'm checking specific facts from the official docs against my deliverable, starting with how environments are represented in the MRT API. The official docs confirm environment variables are a real MRT feature managed per environment, and my references to custom vars like `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID` set through Runtime Admin align with that. On cookies, the official docs note they're not supported by default and require `allow_cookies` enabled in PWA Kit 3.1.0+, which matches my mention of httpOnly cookies and the `localAllowCookies` setting I found in the codebase. This could be important for lower environments too. Beyond the cookie constraint, there are also MRT platform limits I should flag: 6MB request/response size caps, 10KB header limits with 1KB reserved for SCAPI, and execution timeouts of 20 seconds in production and 16 seconds elsewhere. My doc covers the data consumption side well but doesn't address these MRT platform constraints, which are actually part of what defines MRT's capabilities.

I'm also noticing the doc doesn't mention supported regions—Sydney (ap-southeast-2) is relevant for Zimmermann since they're in Australia. And I should verify the proxy's actual purpose: it's meant to speed up API requests, which the official documentation confirms. me clarify the distinction: the generic proxy endpoint forwards requests without injecting credentials—SCAPI relies on the SLAS bearer token from the client. The server-side secret that stays hidden is the SLAS client secret, which is only used in the private-client token exchange through a specific proxy endpoint. My documentation overstates what the proxy does by claiming it "attaches server-only credentials"; the official framing focuses on speed and request modification, not credential injection. This is a precision issue worth refining.

I'm also noticing the CLI tooling: the official admin docs reference `b2c mrt` commands and `sfcc-ci`, while my doc mentions `pwa-kit-dev push` and `sfcc-ci instance:import`. Both sets are valid, though I should check if there's a clearer alignment with what the official docs emphasize.

But the real issue I'm uncovering is that the Managed Runtime API actually exists in practice, yet the documentation seems to deny or omit it entirely. That's the core finding I need to address—the doc should acknowledge the MRT Admin API exists and be explicit about what's in scope versus what's not.

Looking back at the ticket itself, the request is specifically about "product, pricing, and category data consumption," which points directly to SCAPI as the relevant tool. The MRT Admin API handles deployment and infrastructure management, not data consumption, so it falls outside the ticket's actual intent. My documentation correctly served that purpose, but the framing around "MRT API Capabilities" might be creating confusion about what's actually being documented.

I should clarify the distinction upfront: acknowledge that "Managed Runtime" encompasses both the Admin API (for CI/CD and platform administration) and the commerce APIs accessed through MRT's proxy layer, then explain why this spike focuses specifically on the data-consumption side rather than the administrative capabilities.

Now I'm structuring the audit report to be rigorous and honest—laying out what was built against the ticket requirements and internal knowledge, then comparing it to the official SFCC documentation to identify any gaps or misalignments.

For Audit A, I'm validating the four tasks and definition of done against the codebase, Confluence, and Jira records. The coverage is strong overall, with the ticket intent well-met and most of the DoD satisfied, though there are a couple of items gated by external dependencies.

For Audit B, I'm diving into the official MRT documentation and finding a significant discrepancy: the ticket claims MRT isn't an API, but the official docs clearly describe a real Managed Runtime Admin API, so that framing needs correction.

On the positive side, the proxy mechanism I documented checks out against the official specs. However, there's a notable gap—the ticket doesn't address key MRT platform constraints like request/response size limits, execution timeouts, bundle size restrictions, supported regions, and environment variables that are fundamental to how MRT actually operates.

Beyond that, there are a couple of precision issues worth flagging: the docs don't mention that cookies require explicit enablement through `allow_cookies` configuration, which is critical for flows like SLAS refresh-token handling, and the claim about the proxy letting MRT attach server-only credentials oversimplifies what's actually a credential-handling feature specific to certain configurations.

Since the user asked me to audit and report findings rather than auto-edit, I should compile these into a clear recommendations list and offer to apply fixes if they want, rather than modifying the doc unilaterally. B1 is definitely a correctness issue worth flagging — saying "MRT is not an API" is factually wrong since the Managed Runtime API exists and is documented. The spirit of my point (that the data APIs are SCAPI) is correct, but the phrasing itself would immediately get caught by someone familiar with Salesforce Commerce Cloud. The MRT API handles administrative functions like environments, deployments, redirects, and access control, so it's accurate to call it admin-focused, but I can't claim it doesn't exist.

There's a deeper relationship I'm noticing between the codebase's proxy configuration and the Runtime Admin setup — the proxyConfigs defined locally in the code work for development, but in production those same proxies need to be registered in Runtime Admin through the MRT API. The `/mobify/proxy/api` and `/ocapi` proxies aren't just code-level settings; they're infrastructure that has to be configured on both sides.

I should also verify my documentation against the official constraints. The performance and caching claims in my section 3.1.4 align with what the official docs say about edge/CDN/proxy acceleration, so that checks out. And I need to make sure my characterization of MRT as "the PWA Kit Node server" matches what the official overview actually states about MRT providing deployment, hosting, and monitoring infrastructure.

Looking back at the ticket requirements, I covered all four tasks and the definition of done, with two items gated appropriately. My prior validation confirmed accuracy against the codebase and internal docs, so the audit is largely passing. But I realize one of the ticket tasks specifically asks to document available MRT APIs—endpoint structure, payload format, authentication, and data available—and my current doc only partially addresses this.

I documented the SCAPI endpoints for data consumption, but I didn't include the MRT Admin API endpoints. Depending on how literally "MRT APIs" is interpreted, Task 1 could be seen as incomplete. Given the objective focuses on data consumption, it's defensible, but I should flag this tension in the report: Task 1 is complete for the data-consumption scope, incomplete if the literal MRT Admin API is required. I'll recommend clarifying the scope explicitly.

Now I'm drafting the findings report—I'll lead with the headline finding, include a coverage matrix for the audit, list findings with severity levels, and keep it concise but thorough.

I need to be precise with document references and avoid fabrication. I'll use severity labels consistently: BLOCKER, SHOULD-FIX, and NICE-TO-HAVE.

For B1 (the framing that MRT is not an API when the MRT Admin API actually exists), I'm marking this as SHOULD-FIX with high priority—it's the document's headline claim and it's technically incorrect, though the data-consumption content remains valid. For B3 (missing MRT platform capabilities and constraints), that's also SHOULD-FIX since it's important context before final publication.

B4 about cookies and the allow_cookies dependency for SLAS refresh is borderline—it's genuinely useful for lower-environment setup and represents a real dependency in the auth flow, so I could justify SHOULD-FIX, but I'll mark it NICE-TO-HAVE and let the user weigh in. B5 about the proxy credentials overstatement is NICE-TO-HAVE for precision.

B6 on targets terminology is NICE-TO-HAVE since proxies are also an admin/env setting. The positives are solid—the proxy mechanism, environment variable model, TLS, and push targets all check out against the official docs, which builds confidence.

Now I'm ready to write the report itself. I'll keep the tone direct and professional rather than leaning on the teaching analogy we've been using, and I'll be careful to cite specific line references from the official docs where they support the findings—like the Admin Tools section, targets definition, proxy endpoint, environment variables, cookies, request limits, and execution time constraints.

I don't need additional tool calls since I've already reviewed both documents thoroughly. I should also update my memory with the key finding about MRT having a real Admin API separate from the data path, since that's a meaningful refinement to the project understanding that future sessions should know about. I need to refine the memory file's crux statement to accurately reflect that MRT has both a hosting/proxy layer and an Admin API, rather than dismissing it as just a proxy layer. I need to find and update that exact string in the memory file, changing "MRT is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer, not an API" to clarify that there is an admin API but it's not for commerce data. Once I locate and edit that passage, I'll be ready to write out the report.

SFCC-122 "Spike: Document SFCC MRT API Capabilities" — Jira Spike, project SFCC (zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net), label Squad-A, High, **In Progress**, assigned to Marcel, reported by Jasmijn Tsang. Sibling spikes: SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync, Victor Crisostomo, Ready for Dev), SFCC-123 (Contentful design, Jhoan Rose, In Progress). Board spike house style: Objective / Background / Tasks / Definition of Done (see [[f2r-spike]]).

Objective: document the MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs available for product, category, and pricing so the squad knows what can be built/tested in lower environments while MuleSoft is not yet ready. Background note: "Angelo (=Marcel) to set up session with Mani." Mani = Manikandan Ramachandran (owns SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments epic).

**Crux finding (the reframe the spike needs):** MRT is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer, not an API. Product/category/pricing reach the PWA via **SCAPI Shopper APIs** (shopper-products v1, shopper-search v1, shopper-promotions v1) proxied through MRT (`/mobify/proxy/api`, shortCode `qmyt7hks`), using `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` v5.2.0 hooks with SLAS private-client auth. OCAPI is a proxied fallback (`/mobify/proxy/ocapi`, dev sandbox `bkzk-002`). MuleSoft does NOT serve product/price to the PWA — its role there is the server-to-server AP21→MuleSoft→SFCC catalogue import (OCAPI Data API or SFTP). Price is separate: AP21→SFCC via pricebook XML import (sfcc-ci / BM Site Import), and per TSD Price (292388871) there is NO direct MuleSoft price integration; mechanism (SFTP/API/MuleSoft) is TBC. Pricebook IDs: `{site}-{currency}-list-prices`/`-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). So SCAPI is fully capable NOW; the real blocker is that SFCC has no catalog/price data yet because that MuleSoft feed isn't built.

**Unblock lower envs:** load catalog + pricebook data into the SFCC sandbox via BM or OCAPI Data API so the PWA can consume via SCAPI immediately. Sample-catalog tooling (`data/sample/catalogs`, `data:import:sample`) is NOT in zimmermann-pwa — it lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo (per Confluence TSD Product page 292061208). The PWA repo only consumes.

**Permanent vs workaround:** SCAPI-via-MRT (consumption) + MuleSoft catalogue/pricebook feed (population) are permanent. Manual/sample catalog load into sandbox is the temporary workaround. OCAPI fallback is semi-permanent (anything SCAPI doesn't cover).

# SFCC-122 Audit: Findings

Two audits below. Headline: the deliverable is **accurate and complete for the ticket's *intent*** (data consumption), but the official MRT docs expose **one framing error that must be fixed** before final publish, plus a scope gap.

---

## Audit A — Deliverable vs ticket + codebase/Confluence/Jira

Coverage against the four tasks and the DoD:

| Ticket requirement | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Task 1: document available MRT APIs (endpoints, payload, auth, data) | ✅ for the data reading; ⚠️ for the literal reading | Fully documents **SCAPI** (the data APIs). Does **not** document the literal **MRT Admin API** — see Finding B1. |
| Task 2: what serves product/category/pricing in lower envs now | ✅ | SCAPI works now; blocker is empty data; unblock steps given. |
| Task 3: limitations/gaps for MuleSoft | ✅ | Honest, cross-referenced to Confluence open items. |
| Task 4: permanent vs workaround | ✅ | Defensible classification. |
| DoD: documented inventory, sufficient to unblock BM config + FE dev | ✅ FE / ⚠️ partial BM | Two items externally gated (catalogue IDs + sandbox data state → Mani). |

**Consistency with codebase/Confluence/Jira:** clean. This was hardened over the two earlier validation passes (price decoupled from MuleSoft, `storefront-catalog-eu` reframed, dep-type corrected, pricebook detail added, line refs verified, Jira DoD matched verbatim). No new contradictions found.

**Audit A verdict:** the deliverable satisfies the ticket's *intent* well. Its one weakness is inherited from the ticket's own ambiguous title, which Audit B exposes.

---

## Audit B — Deliverable vs official SFCC MRT docs

### 🔴 B1 — SHOULD-FIX (top priority): "MRT is not an API" is factually wrong
Our doc's headline reframe (TL;DR #1, §3.1) states *"MRT is the hosting and proxy layer, **not an API**."* The official Overview says otherwise:

> *"The **Managed Runtime API**, a REST API that offers the same functionality as the web-based [Runtime Admin] tool and some additional capabilities."* (Overview, Admin Tools, lines 122-129)

There genuinely **is** a "Managed Runtime API" — the **`mrt-admin`** REST API. It's just an **administration/deployment** API (environments a.k.a. "targets", bundles, deploy, redirects, proxies, env vars, CDN invalidation, access-control headers, certificates, users, production flag), **not** a commerce-data API.

So "MRT API capabilities" has **two legitimate readings**, and our doc silently picked one while denying the other exists:
- **(A) The MRT Admin API** — platform/CI-CD administration. *Real, but out of scope for this spike.*
- **(B) APIs reached *through* the MRT proxy** — SCAPI/OCAPI serving product/price/category. *What our doc covers.*

**Why it matters:** the ticket's Objective ("product, pricing, and category data consumption") confirms the *intent* is (B), so our substance is right. But an SFCC-literate reader (or Mani) will immediately catch "MRT is not an API" as wrong and distrust the doc. **Fix:** replace the flat denial with a short "two readings" clarification — acknowledge the MRT Admin API (A), state it's platform admin / CI-CD and out of scope, and explain the spike targets (B) because that's the data question.

### 🟠 B2 — SHOULD-FIX: no coverage of MRT's own platform capabilities/constraints
For a doc literally titled *"MRT API Capabilities,"* it omits MRT's actual platform capabilities and limits, several of which affect the storefront directly:
- **Render execution timeout: 20s prod / 16s non-prod** (Overview 173) — relevant to any slow SCAPI/MuleSoft call.
- **Request/response ≤ 6 MB; header budget 10,240 bytes** with **1,000 reserved for SCAPI** (Overview 154-156).
- **Cookies off by default** (see B3), bundle size limits, static-asset content-type allowlist (Overview 178-179).
- **Edge services**: WAF, proxy, CDN, request-processor edge functions (Overview 109-118).
- **Supported regions** incl. `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney) — relevant for AU (Admin 338).
- **Built-in env vars**: `DEPLOY_TARGET`, `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`, `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` (Overview 105-107).

**Fix:** add a short "MRT platform capabilities & constraints" section (even half a page), or explicitly scope it out with a pointer. Right now it's simply absent.

### 🟡 B3 — NICE-TO-HAVE (but real): cookies are off by default on MRT
Our §3.1.3 describes SLAS refresh tokens living in `httpOnly` cookies. The official docs say **cookies aren't supported by default** and must be enabled per environment via `allow_cookies` / **Server-Side Cookie Access** (Overview 157; Admin 168, 422). That's a genuine dependency for the auth flow we describe, and a concrete lower-env setup checklist item. Worth one line.

### 🟡 B4 — NICE-TO-HAVE: the proxy "attaches credentials" line is loose
§3.1 says the proxy "lets MRT attach server-only credentials." The official proxy purpose is host-rewrite, caching/speed, and user-agent control (Overview 115, 160-163) — credential/secret handling is specific to the **SLAS private-client proxy endpoint**, not the generic `/mobify/proxy/api`. Minor precision fix so it's not misread.

### ✅ B5 — Validated by the official docs (confidence boosters)
The audit *confirmed* several of our claims against the source of truth:
- **`/mobify/proxy/$name`** is exactly the documented proxy mechanism (Overview 160-163) → our proxy paths are correct.
- **Per-environment variables** as an MRT feature (Overview 101-108, 80) → our env-var model is right.
- **TLS 1.2+**, **push to targets** (`-t <target>` = environment), and the **hosting/monitoring** role of MRT all corroborated.

The deliverable is **substantively correct and useful** — it answers the question the squad actually needs answered (what data can we consume, and why we're blocked). lines: ## TL;DR

-1. **"MRT" is the hosting and proxy layer, not an API.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit Node server. The APIs the storefront actually consumes for product, category, and pricing data are **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached *through* the MRT proxy.

+1. **"MRT API" has two meanings; this spike is about the data one.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit hosting layer. There is a real **Managed Runtime Admin API** (`mrt-admin`) for deploying and administering the storefront (environments, bundles, proxies, redirects, environment variables), but that is platform and CI/CD, not commerce data. The APIs that actually serve **product, category, and pricing** are **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached *through* the MRT proxy. This spike documents the SCAPI path; the Admin API is noted for completeness but is out of scope (see 3.1.0 and 3.1.9).

2. **SCAPI can already serve product, category, and pricing today.** The capability exists now: `shopper-products`, `shopper-search`, and pricebook-aware pricing are wired and proven in this codebase. Standalone `shopper-promotions` is available through the base template and is demonstrated here via `expand=promotions`.

3. **The blocker is empty data, not a missing API.** Product and price data are absent from the lower environments because the source-to-SFCC data feeds have not been built yet: product/catalogue is AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC, and price is AP21 to SFCC via XML pricebook import (mechanism, SFTP / API / MuleSoft, still to be confirmed). That is a data-population problem, owned server-side, not an MRT or SCAPI capability gap.

4. **MuleSoft does not serve product or pricing to the PWA.** The direct PWA to MRT to MuleSoft path is only for orders, returns, and real-time boutique stock. Product and price master data is a separate server-to-server import into SFCC.

### 3.1 Task 1: Review and document the available MRT APIs

#### 3.1.0 Scope note: two meanings of "MRT API"

"Managed Runtime" is the infrastructure that deploys, hosts, and monitors the PWA Kit storefront. Two different things get called "the MRT API":

1. **The Managed Runtime Admin API** (`mrt-admin`): a real REST API that mirrors the Runtime Admin web tool. It creates and configures environments (called *targets* in the API), pushes and deploys bundles, and manages proxies, redirects, environment variables, CDN cache invalidation, access-control headers, certificates, and users. This is platform administration and CI/CD, not commerce data.
2. **The commerce APIs reached *through* the MRT proxy** (`/mobify/proxy/...`): **SCAPI** (and OCAPI), which serve product, category, pricing, search, basket, and orders.

This spike is about **(2)**, because the ticket objective is product, pricing, and category data consumption. **(1)** is platform setup / CI-CD and is out of scope here; it is summarised for reference in 3.1.9.

**How commerce data reaches the storefront.** The browser talks to SFCC through a proxy hosted by Managed Runtime. Nothing calls SFCC directly from a hard-coded backend host; every call goes through an MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/...`), which rewrites the request to the correct backend host and applies MRT's edge caching and security. Secrets such as the SLAS client secret are kept server-side by the private-client proxy endpoint, never in the browser bundle.

#### 3.1.9 The Managed Runtime platform: Admin API and constraints (reference, out of scope)

Included so the "MRT API capabilities" picture is complete, even though this spike's focus is the SCAPI data path.

**Managed Runtime Admin API (`mrt-admin`).** A REST API (with a matching Runtime Admin web tool and `b2c mrt` / `pwa-kit-dev` CLIs) for platform administration and CI/CD, not commerce data. Capabilities include: create and configure environments (targets) and mark them production; push, deploy, and delete bundles; and manage proxies, redirects, environment variables, access-control headers, TLS certificates, users and roles, deployment notifications, and CDN cache invalidation. It matters here only in that our proxies (`api`, `ocapi`) and per-environment variables (`COMMERCE_API_*`, the SLAS client secret, etc.) are configured through this layer, not solely in `config/*.js`.

**Platform constraints that affect the storefront** (from the official MRT docs):

| Constraint | Value |
|---|---|
| App Server render timeout | 20s production, 16s non-production, then HTTP 502 |
| Request / response size | 6 MB max |
| Request line + headers | 10,240 bytes max (approx 1,000 reserved for SCAPI, 1,800 for auth, leaving approx 5,940 for custom headers and cookies) |
| Cookies | Off by default; enable via `allow_cookies` / Server-Side Cookie Access (see 3.1.3) |
| Bundle size | 400 MB max; `ssr_only` + `ssr_shared` files 249 MB max |
| Static assets served | Only specific content types (JS, JSON, CSS, common image types, fonts); anything else served externally |
| Reserved path prefix | `/mobify` (`/mobify/ping`, `/mobify/redirect/$path`, `/mobify/proxy/$name`) |
| Built-in env vars | `DEPLOY_TARGET`, `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`, `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` |
| Edge services | WAF, API proxy, CDN, request-processor edge functions |
| Region (AU-relevant) | `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney) supported, `ap-southeast-1` (Singapore) as backup |

**Platform constraints that affect the storefront** (from the official MRT docs):

| Constraint | Value |
|---|---|
| App Server render timeout | 20s production, 16s non-production, then HTTP 502 |
| Request / response size | 6 MB max |
| Request line + headers | 10,240 bytes max (approx 1,000 reserved for SCAPI, 1,800 for auth, leaving approx 5,940 for custom headers and cookies) |
| Cookies | Off by default; enable via `allow_cookies` / Server-Side Cookie Access (see 3.1.3) |
| Bundle size | 400 MB max; `ssr_only` + `ssr_shared` files 249 MB max |

| Reserved path prefix | `/mobify` (`/mobify/ping`, `/mobify/redirect/$path`, `/mobify/proxy/$name`) |
| Built-in env vars | `DEPLOY_TARGET`, `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`, `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` |
| Edge services | WAF, API proxy, CDN, request-processor edge functions |
| Region (AU-relevant) | `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney) supported, `ap-southeast-1` (Singapore) as backup |
