    "content": {
      "value": "This page documents the alternative catalogue sync design using **SCAPI Admin APIs** instead of WebDAV file-based import. It covers the same three data domains — Product, Price, and Inventory — and follows the same section structure as the file-based design for direct comparison.

> **Context:** The file-based design (WebDAV + import job) is the recommended approach for Zimmermann's catalogue scale. This SCAPI Admin API design is documented as the alternative pattern — applicable for real-time single-product event scenarios or if the file-based approach is ruled out. See the [parent page comparison](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) for the full pro/con trade-off.

Related pages: - [TSD: Catalogue Sync — Product, Price & Inventory (MuleSoft → SFCC)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) — file-based design - [TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208) - [TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312377345) - [TSD: Price — SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292388871)

---

1-overview1. Overview
---------------------

In the SCAPI Admin API pattern, MuleSoft calls SFCC REST endpoints directly per product or inventory record. Each domain uses a dedicated SCAPI Admin API family.

> **API Note:** OCAPI is deprecated. All SFCC Admin API calls use **SCAPI Admin APIs** authenticated via **Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2)** — client credentials grant.
>
> ⚠️ **Price sync exception:** There is no published SCAPI Admin API or verified OCAPI endpoint for writing pricebook entries programmatically. **Price sync must always use the file-based pricebook XML import** (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import` job) regardless of which pattern is chosen for products and inventory. See Section 5.

| Domain | Mechanism | SCAPI API | Auth | API Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Product | SCAPI Admin API (per product/variant) | Products Admin API — `POST` / `PUT` | AmOAuth2 | [Products](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/products) |
| Price | **File-based only** — WebDAV + import job | No SCAPI API exists | AmOAuth2 (WebDAV) | — |
| Inventory | SCAPI Admin API (per record) | Inventory Lists API — `PUT` / `PATCH` | AmOAuth2 | [Inventory Lists](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/inventory-lists) |

**SCAPI Admin API base URL:**Defaultnonehttps://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com

**Auth token acquisition (product and inventory domains):**DefaultnonePOST https://account.demandware.com/dwsso/oauth2/access\_token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
grant\_type=client\_credentials
&client\_id={mulesoftClientId}
&client\_secret={mulesoftClientSecret}

---

2-sequencing-constraints2. Sequencing Constraints
-------------------------------------------------

Unlike the file-based import job which handles sequencing internally, the SCAPI Admin API pattern requires MuleSoft to enforce strict operation order across product and inventory domains. Price sync runs independently via file-based import and does not participate in this sequence.

DefaultnoneFor each style (master product):
STEP 1 — Create or update MASTER product
POST /product/v1/.../products/{catalogId}
STEP 2 — Create or update each VARIANT
POST /product/v1/.../products/{catalogId}
⚠ Must complete after Step 1 — variant fails if master does not exist
STEP 3 — Assign products to CATEGORIES
PUT /product/v1/.../categories/{categoryId}/products/{productId}
⚠ Must complete after Step 1
STEP 4 — Write INVENTORY
PUT /inventory/v1/.../inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}
⚠ Must complete after Step 2 — variant must exist before inventory record
STEP 5 — PRICE SYNC (file-based — independent of above sequence)
Pricebook XML → WebDAV → sfcc-site-archive-import job
Runs on its own schedule
⚠ Variant must exist in SFCC before a pricebook entry for it is valid

---

3-sync-orchestration--mulesoft-flow-product-and-inventory3. Sync Orchestration — MuleSoft Flow (Product and Inventory)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The SCAPI Admin API pattern requires a **separate MuleSoft flow per domain** (product, inventory), each with its own retry logic, error tracking, and partial-success handling. Price sync uses the file-based flow documented in the [parent page](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418).

DefaultnoneAP21 / NewStore (source event or scheduler trigger)
│
▼
MuleSoft
│
├── 1. GET AmOAuth2 TOKEN
│ POST https://account.demandware.com/dwsso/oauth2/access\_token
│ Cache token; refresh before expiry (typically 30 min TTL)
│
├── 2. CHECK PRODUCT EXISTS (product domain only)
│ GET /product/v1/.../products/{catalogId}/{productId}
│ → 200: product exists → use PUT to update
│ → 404: product does not exist → use POST to create
│
├── 3. EXECUTE API CALL
│ POST / PUT per domain (see Sections 4 and 6)
│ Headers: Authorization: Bearer {amOAuth2Token}
│ Content-Type: application/json
│ → 200 / 201: success
│ → 4xx: business error — log, skip record, continue
│ → 429: rate limit — back off and retry
│ → 5xx: server error — retry up to 3 times with exponential back-off
│
├── 4. TRACK RESULT PER RECORD
│ { productId: "success" | "failed" | "skipped" }
│
├── 5. CONTINUE TO NEXT RECORD
│ Do not abort entire batch on a single record failure
│
└── 6. POST-RUN SUMMARY
If any records failed → raise alert via Anypoint monitoring
Store failed record IDs for manual replay or next-run retry

4-product-sync4. Product Sync
-----------------------------

### 41-trigger4.1 Trigger

AP21 product create or update event consumed by MuleSoft. Can be event-driven (real-time per product) or scheduled batch.

### 42-api-endpoints4.2 API Endpoints

| Operation | Method | Endpoint | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create master | `POST` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}` | Product does not exist |
| Update master | `PUT` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}/{productId}` | Product exists |
| Create variant | `POST` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}` | Variant does not exist — after master created |
| Update variant | `PUT` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}/{productId}` | Variant exists |
| Assign to category | `PUT` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/categories/{categoryId}/products/{productId}` | After product created |

### 45-upsert-pattern4.5 Upsert Pattern

SCAPI does not have a native upsert endpoint for products. MuleSoft must check existence before every write:

DefaultnoneGET /product/v1/.../products/{catalogId}/{productId}
→ 200 → PUT (update)

For a batch of 1,000 products × 5 variants = 12,000 API calls (6,000 existence checks + 6,000 writes).

5-price-sync--filebased-only5. Price Sync — File-Based Only
-----------------------------------------------------------

> ⚠️ **No SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook entries.**
>
> This has been confirmed against Salesforce developer documentation — no SCAPI Admin API for pricebook entry writes exists as a published endpoint. OCAPI is deprecated and must not be used for new integrations.
>
> **Price sync must use the file-based pricebook XML import regardless of which pattern is chosen for products and inventory.**

### 51-mechanism5.1 Mechanism

Pricebook XML delivered via WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import` job — identical to the file-based design. See [TSD: Catalogue Sync — Product, Price & Inventory — Section 5](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) for the full specification.

### 52-scope5.2 Scope

Domestic sites only — AU, UK, US, EU. International sites (USIntl, EUIntl, HK, ME) pricing is managed by Global-e.

| Site | List Pricebook ID | Sale Pricebook ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ZimmermannAU | `au-aud-list-prices` | `au-aud-sale-prices` |
| ZimmermannUK | `uk-gbp-list-prices` | `uk-gbp-sale-prices` |
| ZimmermannUS | `us-usd-list-prices` | `us-usd-sale-prices` |
| ZimmermannEU | `eu-eur-list-prices` | `eu-eur-sale-prices` |

### 53-implication-for-hybrid-pattern5.3 Implication for Hybrid Pattern

If Zimmermann selects SCAPI Admin API for product and inventory sync, MuleSoft must still implement the WebDAV + job-trigger flow for price sync. Both flows co-exist:

* **Product + Inventory** → SCAPI Admin API per-record calls
* **Price** → WebDAV pricebook XML + `sfcc-site-archive-import` job

6-inventory-sync6. Inventory Sync
---------------------------------

### 61-trigger6.1 Trigger

Every 15 minutes per region (AU, GB, US). EU, EUIntl, HK, ME coverage to be confirmed — see open item #3.

### 62-source6.2 Source

NewStore S3 availability export → MuleSoft decompresses and transforms to SCAPI Inventory Lists API payloads.

### 63-api-reference6.3 API Reference

[SCAPI Inventory Lists API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/inventory-lists) — Admin API, AmOAuth2 auth.

**Base path:**Defaultnonehttps://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com
/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}

**Required scope:**`sfcc.inventory.availability.rw`

### 64-api-endpoints6.4 API Endpoints

| Operation | Method | Endpoint | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create or update inventory record | `PUT` | `/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}` | Full replace of record |
| Partial update inventory record | `PATCH` | `/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}` | Update specific fields only. Negative allocation amounts are disallowed |
| Get inventory record | `GET` | `/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}` | Read current record before update if needed |
| Delete inventory record | `DELETE` | `/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}` | Remove record entirely |

### 67-put-vs-patch6.7 PUT vs PATCH

Use `PUT` for a full inventory record write from NewStore (all fields known). Use `PATCH` only for targeted partial corrections (e.g. adjusting `allocation` only after a manual stock adjustment). For the standard 15-minute NewStore sync, `PUT` is the correct method.

---

7-rate-limits-and-throttling7. Rate Limits and Throttling
---------------------------------------------------------

| Concern | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Rate limit | SCAPI Admin API: requests per minute per client — confirm exact limit with Salesforce TAM |
| Timeout | SCAPI Admin API: 60-second response timeout per call |
| 429 response | Back off — exponential back-off starting at 5 seconds; retry |
| Parallel calls | Parallelise per domain within rate limit — use Anypoint throttling policy |
| Bulk endpoint | No native bulk endpoint for products or inventory records — each is a separate call |
| Recommended rate | 10 requests/second via Anypoint rate limiting; monitor 429 responses in Anypoint |

---

8-error-handling8. Error Handling
---------------------------------

| Scenario | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| 404 on product existence check | Product does not exist — switch to POST. Not an error |
| 400 Bad Request | Invalid payload — log record ID and error detail; skip; continue; alert on post-run summary |
| 409 Conflict | Concurrent write conflict — retry once after 2-second delay |
| 422 Unprocessable Entity | Business validation failure (e.g. master missing for variant, negative inventory) — log and skip |
| 429 Rate Limited | Exponential back-off: 5s, 10s, 20s; alert if persistent |
| 500 / 503 Server Error | Retry up to 3 times; move to failed queue; alert |
| Token expired | Re-acquire AmOAuth2 token mid-batch; cache and refresh proactively before TTL |
| Negative inventory value | MuleSoft must validate and reject before calling API — negative allocations are disallowed |
| Partial batch failure | Log all failed record IDs; raise Anypoint alert; store for replay |

---

9-operational-comparison-vs-filebased9. Operational Comparison vs File-Based
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Aspect | File-Based (WebDAV + Import Job) | SCAPI Admin API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bulk catalogue load | ✅ Single zip | ❌ Thousands of calls |
| Real-time single product | ❌ Minutes latency | ✅ Seconds |
| Rate limits | ✅ None on import job | ❌ Rate limited |
| Sequencing | ✅ Handled by job | ❌ MuleSoft must enforce |
| Upsert support (product) | ✅ Merge mode native | ❌ GET + POST/PUT per record |
| Inventory write | ✅ XML import | ✅ SCAPI Inventory Lists API (`PUT`/`PATCH`) |
| Negative inventory guard | ✅ Handled by import job | ❌ MuleSoft must validate before call |
| Error visibility | ✅ BM log (job-level + record-level) | ✅ Per-call HTTP response |
| MuleSoft dev effort | Low | High |
| Price sync | ✅ Pricebook XML import | ❌ **No API exists — must use file-based regardless** |
| Fit for Zimmermann scale | ✅ Recommended | ⚠ Product/inventory supplement only — price always file-based |

---

SFCC-122 "Spike: Document SFCC MRT API Capabilities" — Jira Spike, project SFCC (zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net), label Squad-A, High, **In Progress**, assigned to Marcel, reported by Jasmijn Tsang. Sibling spikes: SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync, Victor Crisostomo, Ready for Dev), SFCC-123 (Contentful design, Jhoan Rose, In Progress). Board spike house style: Objective / Background / Tasks / Definition of Done (see [[f2r-spike]]).

Objective: document the MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs available for product, category, and pricing so the squad knows what can be built/tested in lower environments while MuleSoft is not yet ready. Background note: "Angelo (=Marcel) to set up session with Mani." Mani = Manikandan Ramachandran (owns SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments epic).

**Crux finding (the reframe the spike needs):** MRT is primarily the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer. IMPORTANT correction (per official MRT docs, audited 2026-07-22): there IS a real "Managed Runtime API" but it is an ADMIN/deployment REST API (mrt-admin: environments/targets, bundles, deploy, redirects, proxies, env vars, CDN invalidation, access-control headers, certs, users), NOT a commerce-data API. The deliverable's original flat claim "MRT is not an API" was WRONG; corrected via audit fixes B1-B4 (applied 2026-07-23, doc + Confluence page now v3). Accurate framing now in the doc (3.1.0, 3.1.9): the MRT Admin API = platform admin/CI-CD (out of scope for this spike), while product/category/pricing data comes via SCAPI reached through the MRT proxy (/mobify/proxy/api). Audit also added an MRT platform capabilities/constraints table (render timeout 20s/16s, 6MB req/resp, cookies-off-by-default/allow_cookies, bundle limits, reserved /mobify prefix, built-in env vars, edge services, ap-southeast-2 region). Product/category/pricing reach the PWA via **SCAPI Shopper APIs** (shopper-products v1, shopper-search v1, shopper-promotions v1) proxied through MRT (`/mobify/proxy/api`, shortCode `qmyt7hks`), using `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` v5.2.0 hooks with SLAS private-client auth. OCAPI is a proxied fallback (`/mobify/proxy/ocapi`, dev sandbox `bkzk-002`). MuleSoft does NOT serve product/price to the PWA — its role there is the server-to-server AP21→MuleSoft→SFCC catalogue import (OCAPI Data API or SFTP). Price is separate: AP21→SFCC via pricebook XML import (sfcc-ci / BM Site Import), and per TSD Price (292388871) there is NO direct MuleSoft price integration; mechanism (SFTP/API/MuleSoft) is TBC. Pricebook IDs: `{site}-{currency}-list-prices`/`-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). So SCAPI is fully capable NOW; the real blocker is that SFCC has no catalog/price data yet because that MuleSoft feed isn't built.

**Unblock lower envs:** load catalog + pricebook data into the SFCC sandbox via BM or OCAPI Data API so the PWA can consume via SCAPI immediately. Sample-catalog tooling (`data/sample/catalogs`, `data:import:sample`) is NOT in zimmermann-pwa — it lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo (per Confluence TSD Product page 292061208). The PWA repo only consumes.

**Permanent vs workaround:** SCAPI-via-MRT (consumption) + MuleSoft catalogue/pricebook feed (population) are permanent. Manual/sample catalog load into sandbox is the temporary workaround. OCAPI fallback is semi-permanent (anything SCAPI doesn't cover).

Not yet published to Confluence. Publish target (confirmed by Marcel 2026-07-22): parent page "05.1 — Architecture & Solution Design" (id 277577731, space SFCC), as a sibling of "Technical Solution Design – PWA" (256835585); proposed title "TSD: SFCC MRT API Capabilities (Spike SFCC-122)". URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/349437965. NOT yet linked on the Jira ticket and NOT announced to the squad (draft-only). Note: connector creates a live/current page (no native hidden-draft status), so it IS visible in the tree though clearly marked DRAFT. To finalise later: remove the banner + `[DRAFT]` title prefix + `draft` label, fold in Mani's answers, then link on SFCC-122. Two DoD items remain externally gated: exact sandbox catalogue IDs + data state (need Mani), and "shared with squad" (needs Marcel's publish approval). Note: TSD catalogue IDs (`zimmermann-catalog`, `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`) do NOT match repo sample data (`storefront-catalog-eu`) — confirm with Mani.

Key sources: codebase `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` (SCAPI endpoint inventory §4) and `03-mulesoft.md` (PWA-direct MuleSoft reads: orders/returns/boutique stock only). Confluence SFCC space: 292061208 (TSD Product Catalogue), 292388871 (TSD Price/Pricebooks), 320602113 (MuleSoft Open Questions), 256835585 (TSD PWA), 264896514 (Headless build/deploy).

# Verifying Mani's claim + what Victor is for

## Is "most of the information is already documented in Confluence" verified?

**Yes, largely true.** Three of your four asks are genuinely documented, and in *sharper* detail than our current draft. Only one is a real gap. Per-question:

| Your ask to Mani | Documented in Confluence? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Current BM config + `bkzk-002` sandbox** | ✅ **Yes, well** | [Business Manager Configuration Management](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/309657601) (the authoritative one): what's source-controlled (`data/core`: catalogs, pricebook/inventory *shells*, site prefs), what's applied at sandbox creation (`zimmermann-sfcc-admin` GitHub Action: WebDAV + OCAPI settings), what's BM-owned (catalog assignment, search index rebuild). Plus BM checklists: [Catalog & Product Setup](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/339836968), [Price Books](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/340000816). |
| **2. What data is *currently loaded* in lower envs** | ❌ **No** | Design docs describe the *structure* (pricebooks/inventory are explicitly "empty shells, no prices/stock") and *how* to load, but nowhere state the live contents of `bkzk-002` right now. Operational fact, not design. **→ Victor.** |
| **3. How that data was loaded** | ◐ **Mechanism yes; actual execution no** | Mechanism is documented: `data:import:core` via `sfcc-ci`, `data/sample` imported **manually**, a `workflow_dispatch` GitHub Action for dev/sit ([Build & Deployment](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/264896514)), site-archive import ([whiteboard 265256967](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/265256967)). Whether/what was actually run on `bkzk-002` is not recorded. **→ Victor.** |
| **4. Planned approach to load catalog/pricebook before MuleSoft** | ✅ **Yes, definitively** | [TSD: Catalogue Sync (file-based)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) + [SCAPI Admin API alternative](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/315490342): file-based (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`) is **recommended**; **price is always file-based** (no write API exists); OCAPI is **deprecated**; `data/sample` is the manual dev-load path. |

**Verdict:** Mani is right. You can self-serve most of SFCC-122 by reading those pages — you don't need a live session with him.

## This has two consequences for our deliverable

Reading these actually **resolves two of our own open items** and **dates one section**:

1. **Catalogue-ID caveat resolved.** BM Config Management confirms `zimmermann-catalog` (master) and `zimmermann-*-storefront-catalog` **are** the real, source-controlled IDs. Our §3.1.8 "confirm with Mani" caveat can be closed.
2. **Our §3.1.8 loading mechanism is now dated.** We wrote "admin OCAPI Data API (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`)". The newer Confluence guidance says **OCAPI is deprecated**; the real paths are **file-based WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`** (recommended) or **SCAPI Admin API via AmOAuth2** (alternative, products/inventory only). Worth updating. (Note: Confluence is internally inconsistent here — the older TSD Product still says OCAPI Data API — so flag it, don't just silently flip.)

## What you actually need Victor for

Victor is the right person because he owns **SFCC-121 "Validate MuleSoft Sync Process"** — he's hands-on with the sync and the sandbox loading. Everything to ask him is the **operational / current-state** slice that design docs can't contain:

1. **What's actually loaded in `bkzk-002` right now** — has any catalog/product data been imported, or is it just the empty structure? Any sample/test pricing, or empty pricebook shells?
2. **Has `data/core` (and any manual `data/sample`) import actually been run** against `bkzk-002` — by whom, when, and via the GitHub Action or `sfcc-ci` directly?
3. **Is the first-time BM setup done** on the sandbox — storefront catalog assigned per site, search index rebuilt — or still pending? (This is what makes `shopper-search` return results.)
4. **Is there a usable `data/sample` catalog + pricebook** we can import now to unblock front-end work, and **who runs it** — can front-end trigger it, or does he/platform?
5. **SFCC-121 status/timeline** — when the real MuleSoft catalogue feed is expected, so we know how long the interim sample load needs to carry us.
6. **Access** — do we have the sandbox/WebDAV/`sfcc-ci` access (and AmOAuth2 client if using the SCAPI Admin path) to load data ourselves?

---

Want me to (a) **fold the Confluence findings into the deliverable** — close the catalogue-ID caveat, correct the OCAPI/loading-mechanism section, and rewrite §6 so the open questions are just the genuine Victor items — and/or (b) **draft the message to Victor** from the six points above?

This is what "MuleSoft is not yet ready" refers to, and it is not an MRT capability at all. The key distinction is structure versus data:

- **Structure is source-controlled and already defined.** The `sfccworkplace` repo's `data/core/` holds the master catalogue (`catalogs/zimmermann-catalog/`), the per-site storefront catalogues (`catalogs/zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog/`), and pricebook and inventory-list definitions that are **empty shells: structure only, no prices or stock**. It is applied with `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) and is safe to re-run. Instance-level WebDAV and API settings are applied once at sandbox creation by the `zimmermann-sfcc-admin` GitHub Action. First-time Business Manager steps (storefront-catalogue assignment per site, search-index rebuild) are done once in BM.
- **The actual product and price data is what is missing.** It loads one of two ways:
  - **File-based import (recommended for catalogue scale):** product/catalogue and pricebook XML delivered via WebDAV and applied by the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job (run through `sfcc-ci instance:import`). A filtered sample catalogue lives at `data/sample/` and is imported manually for dev and demo bootstrapping.
  - **SCAPI Admin API (alternative, real-time per record):** the SCAPI Products and Inventory Lists Admin APIs, authenticated via Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2, client credentials), base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`. Suited to single-product event scenarios, not bulk load.
- **Price is always file-based.** No SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook entries (and OCAPI is deprecated), so prices always load as Pricebook XML via WebDAV plus `sfcc-site-archive-import`, whichever pattern is used for products. There is no direct MuleSoft price integration today; the AP21-to-SFCC price delivery mechanism is still to be confirmed. Pricebook IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`, `au-aud-sale-prices`; the sale pricebook parents the list pricebook).
- **Catalogue IDs (confirmed).** Master `zimmermann-catalog`; storefront `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`. These are the real, source-controlled IDs in `data/core/catalogs/` per Business Manager Configuration Management. (The `storefront-catalog-eu` string elsewhere in the PWA repo is a `shop.id` field in a sample MuleSoft order payload, not an SFCC catalogue definition.)
- **Product IDs:** master = `stylecode` (e.g. `4673TS251`); variant = `stylecode + colourcode + sizecode`. The master-catalogue-to-storefront-category assignment is set in Business Manager and cannot be set via XML import.

Note on OCAPI: Salesforce guidance moves these admin and import operations to SCAPI Admin APIs; OCAPI is deprecated. Older TSD pages that reference an OCAPI Data API path predate this and should be read with that in mind.

Source: Confluence "Business Manager Configuration Management" (309657601), "TSD: Catalogue Sync (file-based)" (312508418) and "SCAPI Admin API alternative" (315490342), "TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" (292061208), "TSD: Price, SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e" (292388871).

+  - **SCAPI Admin API (alternative, real-time per record):** the SCAPI Products and Inventory Lists Admin APIs, authenticated via Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2, client credentials), base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`. Suited to single-product event scenarios, not bulk load.

+- **Price is always file-based.** No SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook entries (and OCAPI is deprecated), so prices always load as Pricebook XML via WebDAV plus `sfcc-site-archive-import`, whichever pattern is used for products. There is no direct MuleSoft price integration today; the AP21-to-SFCC price delivery mechanism is still to be confirmed. Pricebook IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`, `au-aud-sale-prices`; the sale pricebook parents the list pricebook).

+- **Catalogue IDs (confirmed).** Master `zimmermann-catalog`; storefront `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`. These are the real, source-controlled IDs in `data/core/catalogs/` per Business Manager Configuration Management. (The `storefront-catalog-eu` string elsewhere in the PWA repo is a `shop.id` field in a sample MuleSoft order payload, not an SFCC catalogue definition.)

+- **Product IDs:** master = `stylecode` (e.g. `4673TS251`); variant = `stylecode + colourcode + sizecode`. The master-catalogue-to-storefront-category assignment is set in Business Manager and cannot be set via XML import.
-Source: Confluence "TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" and "TSD: Price, SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e".

+Note on OCAPI: Salesforce guidance moves these admin and import operations to SCAPI Admin APIs; OCAPI is deprecated. Older TSD pages that reference an OCAPI Data API path predate this and should be read with that in mind.

content.content:
1	# SFCC-122: SFCC MRT API Capabilities
2	
3	**Spike deliverable, Squad-A**
4	
5	| | |
6	|---|---|
7	| Jira | SFCC-122 (Spike, High, In Progress) |
8	| Assignee | Marcel Angelo Navarro |
9	| Reporter | Jasmijn Tsang |
10	| Related | SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync), SFCC-123 (Contentful design), SFCC-1 (Platform Setup & Environments, owner: M. Ramachandran) |
11	| Status of this doc | Draft for squad review |
12	| Last updated | 2026-07-23 |
13	
14	---
15	
16	## TL;DR
17	
18	1. **"MRT API" has two meanings; this spike is about the data one.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit hosting layer. There is a real **Managed Runtime Admin API** (`mrt-admin`) for deploying and administering the storefront (environments, bundles, proxies, redirects, environment variables), but that is platform and CI/CD, not commerce data. The APIs that actually serve **product, category, and pricing** are **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached *through* the MRT proxy. This spike documents the SCAPI path; the Admin API is noted for completeness but is out of scope (see 3.1.0 and 3.1.9).
19	2. **SCAPI can already serve product, category, and pricing today.** The capability exists now: `shopper-products`, `shopper-search`, and pricebook-aware pricing are wired and proven in this codebase. Standalone `shopper-promotions` is available through the base template and is demonstrated here via `expand=promotions`.
20	3. **The blocker is empty data, not a missing API.** Product and price data are absent from the lower environments because the source-to-SFCC data feeds have not been built yet: product/catalogue is AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC, and price is AP21 to SFCC via XML pricebook import (mechanism, SFTP / API / MuleSoft, still to be confirmed). That is a data-population problem, owned server-side, not an MRT or SCAPI capability gap.
21	4. **MuleSoft does not serve product or pricing to the PWA.** The direct PWA to MRT to MuleSoft path is only for orders, returns, and real-time boutique stock. Product and price master data is a separate server-to-server import into SFCC.
22	5. **To unblock lower-environment build and test now:** load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox (Business Manager or the OCAPI Data API), confirm the BM site, catalogue, and pricebook assignment, then the PWA consumes it via SCAPI with no code change.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 1. Objective
27	
28	Document the SFCC MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs relevant to the Zimmermann storefront build, so the squad has a clear picture of what is available for product, pricing, and category data consumption before MuleSoft is ready. This lets the squad determine what can be built and tested in lower environments in the meantime.
29	
30	## 2. Background
31	
32	- Base Business Manager configuration is in place on the SFCC sandbox, but product and price data are currently missing because MuleSoft is not yet ready.
33	- Understanding the MRT API capabilities tells the squad what can be built and tested in lower environments while that feed is being built.
34	- M. Ramachandran (owner of SFCC-1, Platform Setup & Environments) directed this work to the existing Confluence documentation (referenced throughout, see Sources) and to Victor Crisostomo (SFCC-121) for the current sandbox state; the data-loading approach itself is documented (sections 3.1.8 and 4).
35	- The storefront is a PWA Kit application (`zimmermann-pwa`) hosted on Managed Runtime, template-extending `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, consuming commerce data from SFCC and editorial content from Contentful.
36	
37	## 3. Tasks and findings
38	
39	### 3.1 Task 1: Review and document the available MRT APIs
40	
41	#### 3.1.0 Scope note: two meanings of "MRT API"
42	
43	"Managed Runtime" is the infrastructure that deploys, hosts, and monitors the PWA Kit storefront. Two different things get called "the MRT API":
44	
45	1. **The Managed Runtime Admin API** (`mrt-admin`): a real REST API that mirrors the Runtime Admin web tool. It creates and configures environments (called *targets* in the API), pushes and deploys bundles, and manages proxies, redirects, environment variables, CDN cache invalidation, access-control headers, certificates, and users. This is platform administration and CI/CD, not commerce data.
46	2. **The commerce APIs reached *through* the MRT proxy** (`/mobify/proxy/...`): **SCAPI** (and OCAPI), which serve product, category, pricing, search, basket, and orders.
47	
48	This spike is about **(2)**, because the ticket objective is product, pricing, and category data consumption. **(1)** is platform setup / CI-CD and is out of scope here; it is summarised for reference in 3.1.9.
49	
50	**How commerce data reaches the storefront.** The browser talks to SFCC through a proxy hosted by Managed Runtime. Nothing calls SFCC directly from a hard-coded backend host; every call goes through an MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/...`), which rewrites the request to the correct backend host and applies MRT's edge caching and security. Secrets such as the SLAS client secret are kept server-side by the private-client proxy endpoint, never in the browser bundle.
51	
52	```
53	Browser (React, SSR + CSR)
54	   |  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
55	   v
56	MRT proxy  /mobify/proxy/api    -->  SCAPI  (Shopper APIs): product, category, price, search, promotions, basket, orders, customers
57	           /mobify/proxy/ocapi  -->  OCAPI  (configured; fallback for gaps; not currently called from app code)
58	           /mobify/proxy/mulesoft --> MuleSoft (orders, returns, boutique stock ONLY; designed, not yet wired)
59	   v
60	SFCC realm (sandbox bkzk-002 in Dev)
61	```
62	
63	The single SDK `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (v5.2.0) handles every SFCC call: SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching. Verified in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (CommerceApiProvider wiring) and consumed via hooks such as `useProduct` and `useProductSearch`.
64	
65	#### 3.1.1 SCAPI Shopper APIs (primary path for product, category, pricing)
66	
67	Reached at MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api` (`config/default.js:131`). These are the APIs that serve the data this spike is about.
68	
69	| API family | Path root | Serves | Verbs |
70	|---|---|---|---|
71	| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail, master/variant resolution, images, prices on the product | GET |
72	| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort, suggestions | GET |
73	| Shopper Promotions | `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | Active promotions, coupon validation | GET |
74	| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | Guest and registered auth, token lifecycle | GET, POST |
75	| Shopper Baskets | `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*` | Basket / cart lifecycle, line items | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE |
76	| Shopper Orders | `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*` | Order placement and lookup of the just-placed order (SFCC-owned checkouts). Order history and detail come from MuleSoft, not SCAPI (see 3.1.6) | POST, GET |
77	| Shopper Customers | `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references | GET, POST, PATCH |
78	
79	Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 4.
80	
81	**Pricing is fully supported through SCAPI.** The canonical query in the codebase (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:52-58`) uses `useProductSearch` with `refine: ['cgid=<categoryId>', 'htype=master']` and `expand: ['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties']`, `perPricebook: true`, `allVariationProperties: true`. This demonstrates category refinement plus pricebook-aware pricing and promotion expansion working end to end, given data exists.
82	
83	#### 3.1.2 Endpoint structure, base URL, and environments
84	
85	- **SCAPI base host:** `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, proxied via `/mobify/proxy/api`. Verified: `config/default.js:210` host `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`.
86	- **Instance identifiers** (non-secret; injected from env into the SDK provider at `config/default.js:132-137`):
87	  - `shortCode`: `qmyt7hks`
88	  - `organizationId`: `f_ecom_bkzk_002` (realm/instance `bkzk_002`)
89	  - `siteId`: `ZimmermannAU` (default). The app defines 10 PWA storefront sites backed by 7 distinct SFCC sites (the four EU-domestic locales share SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`); see `config/sites.overlay.js`.
90	  - `clientId`: SLAS client ID (public identifier, held in `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID`)
91	- **Per-environment config:** `config/dev.js`, `test.js`, `sit.js`, `staging.js`, `uat.js`, `production.js` each override `proxyConfigs`. The SCAPI host stays constant (`qmyt7hks...`); the OCAPI host changes per tier (Dev to `bkzk-002.dx...`, Prod to `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`).
92	- **Env switching:** `npm run env -- <tier>` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`); deploy per tier via `npm run push:<tier>`, which runs `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`.
93	- MRT environment variables are managed per environment in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase (Confluence: Technical Solution Design, PWA).
94	
95	#### 3.1.3 Authentication
96	
97	- **SLAS private-client flow** issues a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper token (after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs carrying customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and a refresh token.
98	- **Secrets stay server-side.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser; the authorisation-code exchange is proxied through the MRT private-client endpoint. The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain in the bundle as public identifiers. Confirmed in `overrides/app/ssr.js:52` (`useSLASPrivateClient: true`) and `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:132,147-148`.
99	- **Refresh tokens** live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies set by the SSR layer; browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token.
100	- **MRT dependency:** cookies are off by default on Managed Runtime. This refresh-token cookie flow requires **Server-Side Cookie Access** (the environment's `allow_cookies` setting) to be enabled per environment, via Runtime Admin or the Admin API, on PWA Kit 3.1.0 or greater. Confirm it is on for each lower environment.
101	- **Multi-site tokens are channel-scoped.** A token for one site is not valid for another; a storefront switch triggers a fresh server-side authorisation (SLAS Trusted System on Behalf).
102	
103	Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 3.
104	
105	#### 3.1.4 Payload format and query conventions
106	
107	- **Format:** JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+), standard SCAPI response envelopes.
108	- **Every request carries** site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and the SLAS bearer token.
109	- **Efficiency levers used:** `expand=` to pull promotions/variations/prices/images in one call; `fields=` projection to trim payloads; `perPricebook: true` for pricebook-aware pricing; TanStack Query dedup and caching (documented working targets: catalogue stale time ~60s, promotions ~30s, basket 0s, per `01-sfcc.md` section 6; the app-level default `staleTime` is 10s).
110	
111	#### 3.1.5 OCAPI (configured proxy; not currently consumed in app code)
112	
113	- A proxy path `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` is configured (`config/default.js:213-216`, Dev host `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com`) so that any operation not covered by SCAPI can be proxied through MRT with OCAPI credentials held server-side. No OCAPI credentials ever reach the browser.
114	- Current state: OCAPI is **not called from application code**; it is referenced only in host-validation and sync tooling (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/sfcc/*.mjs`). It is a configured capability held in reserve, not an active runtime dependency.
115	- Note the distinction from the import channel below: loading catalogue data (3.1.8) uses a separate, admin-authenticated server-side channel (file-based site-archive import, or the SCAPI Admin API), not the shopper-facing `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` storefront proxy.
116	
117	#### 3.1.6 MuleSoft-direct reads via MRT (not product, category, or pricing)
118	
119	There is a designed direct path `PWA to MRT to MuleSoft` at `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of reads where SFCC adds nothing to the round-trip. It is **scaffolded but not yet wired**: no `mulesoft` entry exists in any `config/*.js`, and the intended mechanism is a server-side `fetch()` from `ssr.js` over a dedicated undici connection pool (`overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts:42-46`, `mulesoftPool`), not a PWA Kit `proxyConfig`. A plain proxyConfig would not suffice, because this path must inject `client_id`/`client_secret` request headers and a session-derived `customer_id` that proxyConfigs cannot add.
120	
121	In scope for this path: order history list, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock (Find in Boutique / BOPIS), GiveX balance check. **Product, category, and pricing are explicitly out of scope for this path.** Source: `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`.
122	
123	#### 3.1.7 Einstein recommendations (adjacent capability)
124	
125	Personalised recommendations use the Einstein API (`config/default.js:140-148`, host `https://api.cquotient.com`), consent-gated, with a static SFCC merchandising-group fallback. Not part of the core product/category/pricing consumption but available through the same app.
126	
127	#### 3.1.8 Catalogue and pricebook population path (server-to-server, the missing piece)
128	
129	This is what "MuleSoft is not yet ready" refers to, and it is not an MRT capability at all. The key distinction is structure versus data:
130	
131	- **Structure is source-controlled and already defined.** The `sfccworkplace` repo's `data/core/` holds the master catalogue (`catalogs/zimmermann-catalog/`), the per-site storefront catalogues (`catalogs/zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog/`), and pricebook and inventory-list definitions that are **empty shells: structure only, no prices or stock**. It is applied with `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) and is safe to re-run. Instance-level WebDAV and API settings are applied once at sandbox creation by the `zimmermann-sfcc-admin` GitHub Action. First-time Business Manager steps (storefront-catalogue assignment per site, search-index rebuild) are done once in BM.
132	- **The actual product and price data is what is missing.** It loads one of two ways:
133	  - **File-based import (recommended for catalogue scale):** product/catalogue and pricebook XML delivered via WebDAV and applied by the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job (run through `sfcc-ci instance:import`). A filtered sample catalogue lives at `data/sample/` and is imported manually for dev and demo bootstrapping.
134	  - **SCAPI Admin API (alternative, real-time per record):** the SCAPI Products and Inventory Lists Admin APIs, authenticated via Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2, client credentials), base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`. Suited to single-product event scenarios, not bulk load.
135	- **Price is always file-based.** No SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook entries (and OCAPI is deprecated), so prices always load as Pricebook XML via WebDAV plus `sfcc-site-archive-import`, whichever pattern is used for products. There is no direct MuleSoft price integration today; the AP21-to-SFCC price delivery mechanism is still to be confirmed. Pricebook IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`, `au-aud-sale-prices`; the sale pricebook parents the list pricebook).
136	- **Catalogue IDs (confirmed).** Master `zimmermann-catalog`; storefront `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`. These are the real, source-controlled IDs in `data/core/catalogs/` per Business Manager Configuration Management. (The `storefront-catalog-eu` string elsewhere in the PWA repo is a `shop.id` field in a sample MuleSoft order payload, not an SFCC catalogue definition.)
137	- **Product IDs:** master = `stylecode` (e.g. `4673TS251`); variant = `stylecode + colourcode + sizecode`. The master-catalogue-to-storefront-category assignment is set in Business Manager and cannot be set via XML import.
138	
139	Note on OCAPI: Salesforce guidance moves these admin and import operations to SCAPI Admin APIs; OCAPI is deprecated. Older TSD pages that reference an OCAPI Data API path predate this and should be read with that in mind.
140	
141	Source: Confluence "Business Manager Configuration Management" (309657601), "TSD: Catalogue Sync (file-based)" (312508418) and "SCAPI Admin API alternative" (315490342), "TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" (292061208), "TSD: Price, SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e" (292388871).
142	
143	#### 3.1.9 The Managed Runtime platform: Admin API and constraints (reference, out of scope)
144	
145	Included so the "MRT API capabilities" picture is complete, even though this spike's focus is the SCAPI data path.
146	
147	**Managed Runtime Admin API (`mrt-admin`).** A REST API (with a matching Runtime Admin web tool and `b2c mrt` / `pwa-kit-dev` CLIs) for platform administration and CI/CD, not commerce data. Capabilities include: create and configure environments (targets) and mark them production; push, deploy, and delete bundles; and manage proxies, redirects, environment variables, access-control headers, TLS certificates, users and roles, deployment notifications, and CDN cache invalidation. It matters here only in that our proxies (`api`, `ocapi`) and per-environment variables (`COMMERCE_API_*`, the SLAS client secret, etc.) are configured through this layer, not solely in `config/*.js`.
148	
149	**Platform constraints that affect the storefront** (from the official MRT docs):
150	
151	| Constraint | Value |
152	|---|---|
153	| App Server render timeout | 20s production, 16s non-production, then HTTP 502 |
154	| Request / response size | 6 MB max |
155	| Request line + headers | 10,240 bytes max (approx 1,000 reserved for SCAPI, 1,800 for auth, leaving approx 5,940 for custom headers and cookies) |
156	| Cookies | Off by default; enable via `allow_cookies` / Server-Side Cookie Access (see 3.1.3) |
157	| Bundle size | 400 MB max; `ssr_only` + `ssr_shared` files 249 MB max |
158	| Static assets served | Only specific content types (JS, JSON, CSS, common image types, fonts); anything else served externally |
159	| Reserved path prefix | `/mobify` (`/mobify/ping`, `/mobify/redirect/$path`, `/mobify/proxy/$name`) |
160	| Built-in env vars | `DEPLOY_TARGET`, `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`, `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` |
161	| Edge services | WAF, API proxy, CDN, request-processor edge functions |
162	| Region (AU-relevant) | `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney) supported, `ap-southeast-1` (Singapore) as backup |
163	
164	Source: official Salesforce docs, Managed Runtime Overview and Managed Runtime Administration.
165	
166	### 3.2 Task 2: Which MRT APIs can serve product, category, and pricing in lower environments now
167	
168	**Answer: SCAPI can, as soon as data exists in the sandbox.** The API capability is not the constraint. `shopper-products`, `shopper-search` (with `cgid` category refinement), and pricebook-aware pricing via `expand=prices` with `perPricebook=true` all work against any populated SFCC instance.
169	
170	The only thing missing in the lower environments is **data in the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks**. Once data is loaded (see section 4), front-end development and testing can proceed against SCAPI with no dependency on the upstream data feeds being finished.
171	
172	| Capability | Available in lower env now? | Depends on |
173	|---|---|---|
174	| Product detail (`shopper-products`) | Yes, once catalogue data is loaded | Sandbox catalogue populated |
175	| Category listing / search (`shopper-search`, `cgid`) | Yes, once catalogue + storefront categories + search index exist | BM catalogue assignment + search index rebuild |
176	| Pricing (`prices`, `perPricebook`) | Yes, once pricebooks are loaded and assigned | Sandbox pricebooks populated + assigned to site |
177	| Promotions (`shopper-promotions`) | Yes, once promotions are configured in BM | BM promotion setup |
178	| Auth (SLAS) | Yes, working now | SLAS client already configured |
179	
180	### 3.3 Task 3: Limitations and gaps to be covered by MuleSoft (or elsewhere)
181	
182	- **No catalogue or price data in the sandbox** until either sample/manual data is loaded or the source-to-SFCC product and price feeds are built (dependency: SFCC-121).
183	- **Catalogue/price freshness and delta handling** (event vs scheduled, sale-price removal signals) are data-feed concerns, not SCAPI concerns.
184	- **MuleSoft real-time rate limits** for the direct-read path are unconfirmed (Confluence "MuleSoft Integration, Open Questions", item G3).
185	- **Delivery mechanism for catalogue import** (OCAPI Data API vs SFTP + import job) and the feed trigger are still open (Confluence TSD Product, open item 1).
186	- **Per-environment SLAS client ID / short code** for non-Dev tiers partly outstanding (`.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 7).
187	- The **MuleSoft direct-read path** (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft`) is not yet wired, so order history, returns, and boutique stock are not consumable from the PWA until it is added and MuleSoft endpoints are provisioned per environment.
188	
189	### 3.4 Task 4: Permanent architecture vs current-state workaround
190	
191	| Element | Classification | Notes |
192	|---|---|---|
193	| SCAPI via MRT proxy for product / category / pricing consumption | **Permanent** | The storefront's supported model for all shopper data |
194	| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** | Standard PWA Kit pattern |
195	| AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC product/catalogue feed (population) | **Permanent** | The intended catalogue data source; not yet built |
196	| AP21 to SFCC price feed via pricebook XML import (population) | **Permanent** | No direct MuleSoft price integration per TSD; mechanism (SFTP / API / MuleSoft) to be confirmed; not yet built |
197	| OCAPI via MRT for operations SCAPI does not cover | **Permanent (semi)** | Configured fallback by design; currently unused; shrinks as SCAPI coverage grows |
198	| PWA to MRT to MuleSoft direct reads (orders, returns, boutique stock) | **Permanent** | Designed, not yet wired |
199	| Manual / sample catalogue and pricebook load into the sandbox | **Workaround** | Current-state only, to unblock lower-env build and test before the permanent product and price feeds exist |
200	
201	## 4. Recommended actions to unblock lower environments
202	
203	1. **Load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox.** Two documented mechanisms (see 3.1.8):
204	   - **Apply the source-controlled structure first:** `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) loads the catalogues and the empty pricebook and inventory shells from the `sfccworkplace` repo's `data/core/`. Safe to re-run.
205	   - **Then load sample product and price data:** import the filtered sample catalogue from `data/sample/` (run manually for dev and demo), and load pricebooks as Pricebook XML via WebDAV plus the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job (`sfcc-ci instance:import` or BM Site Import). IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). A `workflow_dispatch` GitHub Action can run the dev/sit import.
206	   - Note: this tooling lives in the `sfccworkplace` and `zimmermann-sfcc-admin` repos (the PWA repo only consumes). Confirm who runs the import, and our access, with Victor (see section 6).

This is BM-owned, one-time-per-sandbox config (per Business Manager Configuration Management).

# SFCC-122: SFCC MRT API Capabilities

**Spike deliverable, Squad-A**

| | |
|---|---|
| Jira | SFCC-122 (Spike, High, In Progress) |
| Assignee | Marcel Angelo Navarro |
| Reporter | Jasmijn Tsang |
| Related | SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync), SFCC-123 (Contentful design), SFCC-1 (Platform Setup & Environments, owner: M. Ramachandran) |
| Status of this doc | Draft for squad review |
| Last updated | 2026-07-23 |

---

## TL;DR

1. **"MRT API" has two meanings; this spike is about the data one.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit hosting layer. There is a real **Managed Runtime Admin API** (`mrt-admin`) for deploying and administering the storefront (environments, bundles, proxies, redirects, environment variables), but that is platform and CI/CD, not commerce data. The APIs that actually serve **product, category, and pricing** are **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached *through* the MRT proxy. This spike documents the SCAPI path; the Admin API is noted for completeness but is out of scope (see 3.1.0 and 3.1.9).
2. **SCAPI can already serve product, category, and pricing today.** The capability exists now: `shopper-products`, `shopper-search`, and pricebook-aware pricing are wired and proven in this codebase. Standalone `shopper-promotions` is available through the base template and is demonstrated here via `expand=promotions`.
3. **The blocker is empty data, not a missing API.** Product and price data are absent from the lower environments because the source-to-SFCC data feeds have not been built yet: product/catalogue is AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC, and price is AP21 to SFCC via XML pricebook import (mechanism, SFTP / API / MuleSoft, still to be confirmed). That is a data-population problem, owned server-side, not an MRT or SCAPI capability gap.
4. **MuleSoft does not serve product or pricing to the PWA.** The direct PWA to MRT to MuleSoft path is only for orders, returns, and real-time boutique stock. Product and price master data is a separate server-to-server import into SFCC.
5. **To unblock lower-environment build and test now:** load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox (Business Manager or the OCAPI Data API), confirm the BM site, catalogue, and pricebook assignment, then the PWA consumes it via SCAPI with no code change.

---

## 1. Objective

Document the SFCC MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs relevant to the Zimmermann storefront build, so the squad has a clear picture of what is available for product, pricing, and category data consumption before MuleSoft is ready. This lets the squad determine what can be built and tested in lower environments in the meantime.

## 2. Background

- Base Business Manager configuration is in place on the SFCC sandbox, but product and price data are currently missing because MuleSoft is not yet ready.
- Understanding the MRT API capabilities tells the squad what can be built and tested in lower environments while that feed is being built.
- M. Ramachandran (owner of SFCC-1, Platform Setup & Environments) directed this work to the existing Confluence documentation (referenced throughout, see Sources) and to Victor Crisostomo (SFCC-121) for the current sandbox state; the data-loading approach itself is documented (sections 3.1.8 and 4).
- The storefront is a PWA Kit application (`zimmermann-pwa`) hosted on Managed Runtime, template-extending `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, consuming commerce data from SFCC and editorial content from Contentful.

## 3. Tasks and findings

### 3.1 Task 1: Review and document the available MRT APIs

#### 3.1.0 Scope note: two meanings of "MRT API"

"Managed Runtime" is the infrastructure that deploys, hosts, and monitors the PWA Kit storefront. Two different things get called "the MRT API":

1. **The Managed Runtime Admin API** (`mrt-admin`): a real REST API that mirrors the Runtime Admin web tool. It creates and configures environments (called *targets* in the API), pushes and deploys bundles, and manages proxies, redirects, environment variables, CDN cache invalidation, access-control headers, certificates, and users. This is platform administration and CI/CD, not commerce data.
2. **The commerce APIs reached *through* the MRT proxy** (`/mobify/proxy/...`): **SCAPI** (and OCAPI), which serve product, category, pricing, search, basket, and orders.

This spike is about **(2)**, because the ticket objective is product, pricing, and category data consumption. **(1)** is platform setup / CI-CD and is out of scope here; it is summarised for reference in 3.1.9.

**How commerce data reaches the storefront.** The browser talks to SFCC through a proxy hosted by Managed Runtime. Nothing calls SFCC directly from a hard-coded backend host; every call goes through an MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/...`), which rewrites the request to the correct backend host and applies MRT's edge caching and security. Secrets such as the SLAS client secret are kept server-side by the private-client proxy endpoint, never in the browser bundle.

```
Browser (React, SSR + CSR)
   |  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
   v
MRT proxy  /mobify/proxy/api    -->  SCAPI  (Shopper APIs): product, category, price, search, promotions, basket, orders, customers
           /mobify/proxy/ocapi  -->  OCAPI  (configured; fallback for gaps; not currently called from app code)
           /mobify/proxy/mulesoft --> MuleSoft (orders, returns, boutique stock ONLY; designed, not yet wired)
   v
SFCC realm (sandbox bkzk-002 in Dev)
```

The single SDK `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (v5.2.0) handles every SFCC call: SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching. Verified in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (CommerceApiProvider wiring) and consumed via hooks such as `useProduct` and `useProductSearch`.

#### 3.1.1 SCAPI Shopper APIs (primary path for product, category, pricing)

Reached at MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api` (`config/default.js:131`). These are the APIs that serve the data this spike is about.

| API family | Path root | Serves | Verbs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail, master/variant resolution, images, prices on the product | GET |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort, suggestions | GET |
| Shopper Promotions | `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | Active promotions, coupon validation | GET |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | Guest and registered auth, token lifecycle | GET, POST |
| Shopper Baskets | `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*` | Basket / cart lifecycle, line items | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE |
| Shopper Orders | `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*` | Order placement and lookup of the just-placed order (SFCC-owned checkouts). Order history and detail come from MuleSoft, not SCAPI (see 3.1.6) | POST, GET |
| Shopper Customers | `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references | GET, POST, PATCH |

Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 4.

**Pricing is fully supported through SCAPI.** The canonical query in the codebase (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:52-58`) uses `useProductSearch` with `refine: ['cgid=<categoryId>', 'htype=master']` and `expand: ['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties']`, `perPricebook: true`, `allVariationProperties: true`. This demonstrates category refinement plus pricebook-aware pricing and promotion expansion working end to end, given data exists.

#### 3.1.2 Endpoint structure, base URL, and environments

- **SCAPI base host:** `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, proxied via `/mobify/proxy/api`. Verified: `config/default.js:210` host `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`.
- **Instance identifiers** (non-secret; injected from env into the SDK provider at `config/default.js:132-137`):
  - `shortCode`: `qmyt7hks`
  - `organizationId`: `f_ecom_bkzk_002` (realm/instance `bkzk_002`)
  - `siteId`: `ZimmermannAU` (default). The app defines 10 PWA storefront sites backed by 7 distinct SFCC sites (the four EU-domestic locales share SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`); see `config/sites.overlay.js`.
  - `clientId`: SLAS client ID (public identifier, held in `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID`)
- **Per-environment config:** `config/dev.js`, `test.js`, `sit.js`, `staging.js`, `uat.js`, `production.js` each override `proxyConfigs`. The SCAPI host stays constant (`qmyt7hks...`); the OCAPI host changes per tier (Dev to `bkzk-002.dx...`, Prod to `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`).
- **Env switching:** `npm run env -- <tier>` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`); deploy per tier via `npm run push:<tier>`, which runs `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`.
- MRT environment variables are managed per environment in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase (Confluence: Technical Solution Design, PWA).

#### 3.1.3 Authentication

- **SLAS private-client flow** issues a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper token (after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs carrying customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and a refresh token.
- **Secrets stay server-side.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser; the authorisation-code exchange is proxied through the MRT private-client endpoint. The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain in the bundle as public identifiers. Confirmed in `overrides/app/ssr.js:52` (`useSLASPrivateClient: true`) and `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:132,147-148`.
- **Refresh tokens** live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies set by the SSR layer; browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token.
- **MRT dependency:** cookies are off by default on Managed Runtime. This refresh-token cookie flow requires **Server-Side Cookie Access** (the environment's `allow_cookies` setting) to be enabled per environment, via Runtime Admin or the Admin API, on PWA Kit 3.1.0 or greater. Confirm it is on for each lower environment.
- **Multi-site tokens are channel-scoped.** A token for one site is not valid for another; a storefront switch triggers a fresh server-side authorisation (SLAS Trusted System on Behalf).

Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 3.

#### 3.1.4 Payload format and query conventions

- **Format:** JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+), standard SCAPI response envelopes.
- **Every request carries** site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and the SLAS bearer token.
- **Efficiency levers used:** `expand=` to pull promotions/variations/prices/images in one call; `fields=` projection to trim payloads; `perPricebook: true` for pricebook-aware pricing; TanStack Query dedup and caching (documented working targets: catalogue stale time ~60s, promotions ~30s, basket 0s, per `01-sfcc.md` section 6; the app-level default `staleTime` is 10s).

#### 3.1.5 OCAPI (configured proxy; not currently consumed in app code)

- A proxy path `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` is configured (`config/default.js:213-216`, Dev host `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com`) so that any operation not covered by SCAPI can be proxied through MRT with OCAPI credentials held server-side. No OCAPI credentials ever reach the browser.
- Current state: OCAPI is **not called from application code**; it is referenced only in host-validation and sync tooling (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/sfcc/*.mjs`). It is a configured capability held in reserve, not an active runtime dependency.
- Note the distinction from the import channel below: loading catalogue data (3.1.8) uses a separate, admin-authenticated server-side channel (file-based site-archive import, or the SCAPI Admin API), not the shopper-facing `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` storefront proxy.

#### 3.1.6 MuleSoft-direct reads via MRT (not product, category, or pricing)

There is a designed direct path `PWA to MRT to MuleSoft` at `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of reads where SFCC adds nothing to the round-trip. It is **scaffolded but not yet wired**: no `mulesoft` entry exists in any `config/*.js`, and the intended mechanism is a server-side `fetch()` from `ssr.js` over a dedicated undici connection pool (`overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts:42-46`, `mulesoftPool`), not a PWA Kit `proxyConfig`. A plain proxyConfig would not suffice, because this path must inject `client_id`/`client_secret` request headers and a session-derived `customer_id` that proxyConfigs cannot add.

In scope for this path: order history list, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock (Find in Boutique / BOPIS), GiveX balance check. **Product, category, and pricing are explicitly out of scope for this path.** Source: `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`.

#### 3.1.7 Einstein recommendations (adjacent capability)

Personalised recommendations use the Einstein API (`config/default.js:140-148`, host `https://api.cquotient.com`), consent-gated, with a static SFCC merchandising-group fallback. Not part of the core product/category/pricing consumption but available through the same app.

#### 3.1.8 Catalogue and pricebook population path (server-to-server, the missing piece)

This is what "MuleSoft is not yet ready" refers to, and it is not an MRT capability at all. The key distinction is structure versus data:

- **Structure is source-controlled and already defined.** The `sfccworkplace` repo's `data/core/` holds the master catalogue (`catalogs/zimmermann-catalog/`), the per-site storefront catalogues (`catalogs/zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog/`), and pricebook and inventory-list definitions that are **empty shells: structure only, no prices or stock**. It is applied with `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) and is safe to re-run. Instance-level WebDAV and API settings are applied once at sandbox creation by the `zimmermann-sfcc-admin` GitHub Action. First-time Business Manager steps (storefront-catalogue assignment per site, search-index rebuild) are done once in BM.
- **The actual product and price data is what is missing.** It loads one of two ways:
  - **File-based import (recommended for catalogue scale):** product/catalogue and pricebook XML delivered via WebDAV and applied by the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job (run through `sfcc-ci instance:import`). A filtered sample catalogue lives at `data/sample/` and is imported manually for dev and demo bootstrapping.
  - **SCAPI Admin API (alternative, real-time per record):** the SCAPI Products and Inventory Lists Admin APIs, authenticated via Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2, client credentials), base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`. Suited to single-product event scenarios, not bulk load.
- **Price is always file-based.** No SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook entries (and OCAPI is deprecated), so prices always load as Pricebook XML via WebDAV plus `sfcc-site-archive-import`, whichever pattern is used for products. There is no direct MuleSoft price integration today; the AP21-to-SFCC price delivery mechanism is still to be confirmed. Pricebook IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`, `au-aud-sale-prices`; the sale pricebook parents the list pricebook).
- **Catalogue IDs (confirmed).** Master `zimmermann-catalog`; storefront `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`. These are the real, source-controlled IDs in `data/core/catalogs/` per Business Manager Configuration Management. (The `storefront-catalog-eu` string elsewhere in the PWA repo is a `shop.id` field in a sample MuleSoft order payload, not an SFCC catalogue definition.)
- **Product IDs:** master = `stylecode` (e.g. `4673TS251`); variant = `stylecode + colourcode + sizecode`. The master-catalogue-to-storefront-category assignment is set in Business Manager and cannot be set via XML import.

Note on OCAPI: Salesforce guidance moves these admin and import operations to SCAPI Admin APIs; OCAPI is deprecated. Older TSD pages that reference an OCAPI Data API path predate this and should be read with that in mind.

Source: Confluence "Business Manager Configuration Management" (309657601), "TSD: Catalogue Sync (file-based)" (312508418) and "SCAPI Admin API alternative" (315490342), "TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" (292061208), "TSD: Price, SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e" (292388871).

#### 3.1.9 The Managed Runtime platform: Admin API and constraints (reference, out of scope)

Included so the "MRT API capabilities" picture is complete, even though this spike's focus is the SCAPI data path.

**Managed Runtime Admin API (`mrt-admin`).** A REST API (with a matching Runtime Admin web tool and `b2c mrt` / `pwa-kit-dev` CLIs) for platform administration and CI/CD, not commerce data. Capabilities include: create and configure environments (targets) and mark them production; push, deploy, and delete bundles; and manage proxies, redirects, environment variables, access-control headers, TLS certificates, users and roles, deployment notifications, and CDN cache invalidation. It matters here only in that our proxies (`api`, `ocapi`) and per-environment variables (`COMMERCE_API_*`, the SLAS client secret, etc.) are configured through this layer, not solely in `config/*.js`.

**Platform constraints that affect the storefront** (from the official MRT docs):

| Constraint | Value |
|---|---|
| App Server render timeout | 20s production, 16s non-production, then HTTP 502 |
| Request / response size | 6 MB max |
| Request line + headers | 10,240 bytes max (approx 1,000 reserved for SCAPI, 1,800 for auth, leaving approx 5,940 for custom headers and cookies) |
| Cookies | Off by default; enable via `allow_cookies` / Server-Side Cookie Access (see 3.1.3) |
| Bundle size | 400 MB max; `ssr_only` + `ssr_shared` files 249 MB max |
| Static assets served | Only specific content types (JS, JSON, CSS, common image types, fonts); anything else served externally |
| Reserved path prefix | `/mobify` (`/mobify/ping`, `/mobify/redirect/$path`, `/mobify/proxy/$name`) |
| Built-in env vars | `DEPLOY_TARGET`, `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`, `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID` |
| Edge services | WAF, API proxy, CDN, request-processor edge functions |
| Region (AU-relevant) | `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney) supported, `ap-southeast-1` (Singapore) as backup |

Source: official Salesforce docs, Managed Runtime Overview and Managed Runtime Administration.

### 3.2 Task 2: Which MRT APIs can serve product, category, and pricing in lower environments now

**Answer: SCAPI can, as soon as data exists in the sandbox.** The API capability is not the constraint. `shopper-products`, `shopper-search` (with `cgid` category refinement), and pricebook-aware pricing via `expand=prices` with `perPricebook=true` all work against any populated SFCC instance.

The only thing missing in the lower environments is **data in the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks**. Once data is loaded (see section 4), front-end development and testing can proceed against SCAPI with no dependency on the upstream data feeds being finished.

| Capability | Available in lower env now? | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Product detail (`shopper-products`) | Yes, once catalogue data is loaded | Sandbox catalogue populated |
| Category listing / search (`shopper-search`, `cgid`) | Yes, once catalogue + storefront categories + search index exist | BM catalogue assignment + search index rebuild |
| Pricing (`prices`, `perPricebook`) | Yes, once pricebooks are loaded and assigned | Sandbox pricebooks populated + assigned to site |
| Promotions (`shopper-promotions`) | Yes, once promotions are configured in BM | BM promotion setup |
| Auth (SLAS) | Yes, working now | SLAS client already configured |

### 3.3 Task 3: Limitations and gaps to be covered by MuleSoft (or elsewhere)

- **No catalogue or price data in the sandbox** until either sample/manual data is loaded or the source-to-SFCC product and price feeds are built (dependency: SFCC-121).
- **Catalogue/price freshness and delta handling** (event vs scheduled, sale-price removal signals) are data-feed concerns, not SCAPI concerns.
- **MuleSoft real-time rate limits** for the direct-read path are unconfirmed (Confluence "MuleSoft Integration, Open Questions", item G3).
- **Delivery mechanism for catalogue import** (OCAPI Data API vs SFTP + import job) and the feed trigger are still open (Confluence TSD Product, open item 1).
- **Per-environment SLAS client ID / short code** for non-Dev tiers partly outstanding (`.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 7).
- The **MuleSoft direct-read path** (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft`) is not yet wired, so order history, returns, and boutique stock are not consumable from the PWA until it is added and MuleSoft endpoints are provisioned per environment.

### 3.4 Task 4: Permanent architecture vs current-state workaround

| Element | Classification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SCAPI via MRT proxy for product / category / pricing consumption | **Permanent** | The storefront's supported model for all shopper data |
| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** | Standard PWA Kit pattern |
| AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC product/catalogue feed (population) | **Permanent** | The intended catalogue data source; not yet built |
| AP21 to SFCC price feed via pricebook XML import (population) | **Permanent** | No direct MuleSoft price integration per TSD; mechanism (SFTP / API / MuleSoft) to be confirmed; not yet built |
| OCAPI via MRT for operations SCAPI does not cover | **Permanent (semi)** | Configured fallback by design; currently unused; shrinks as SCAPI coverage grows |
| PWA to MRT to MuleSoft direct reads (orders, returns, boutique stock) | **Permanent** | Designed, not yet wired |
| Manual / sample catalogue and pricebook load into the sandbox | **Workaround** | Current-state only, to unblock lower-env build and test before the permanent product and price feeds exist |

## 4. Recommended actions to unblock lower environments

1. **Load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox.** Two documented mechanisms (see 3.1.8):
   - **Apply the source-controlled structure first:** `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) loads the catalogues and the empty pricebook and inventory shells from the `sfccworkplace` repo's `data/core/`. Safe to re-run.
