SFCC-122 "Spike: Document SFCC MRT API Capabilities" — Jira Spike, project SFCC (zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net), label Squad-A, High, **In Progress**, assigned to Marcel, reported by Jasmijn Tsang. Sibling spikes: SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync, Victor Crisostomo, Ready for Dev), SFCC-123 (Contentful design, Jhoan Rose, In Progress). Board spike house style: Objective / Background / Tasks / Definition of Done (see [[f2r-spike]]).

Objective: document the MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs available for product, category, and pricing so the squad knows what can be built/tested in lower environments while MuleSoft is not yet ready. Background note: "Angelo (=Marcel) to set up session with Mani." Mani = Manikandan Ramachandran (owns SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments epic).

**Crux finding (the reframe the spike needs):** MRT is primarily the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer. IMPORTANT correction (per official MRT docs, audited 2026-07-22): there IS a real "Managed Runtime API" but it is an ADMIN/deployment REST API (mrt-admin: environments/targets, bundles, deploy, redirects, proxies, env vars, CDN invalidation, access-control headers, certs, users), NOT a commerce-data API. The deliverable's original flat claim "MRT is not an API" was WRONG; corrected via audit fixes B1-B4 (applied 2026-07-23, doc + Confluence page now v3). Accurate framing now in the doc (3.1.0, 3.1.9): the MRT Admin API = platform admin/CI-CD (out of scope for this spike), while product/category/pricing data comes via SCAPI reached through the MRT proxy (/mobify/proxy/api). Audit also added an MRT platform capabilities/constraints table (render timeout 20s/16s, 6MB req/resp, cookies-off-by-default/allow_cookies, bundle limits, reserved /mobify prefix, built-in env vars, edge services, ap-southeast-2 region). Product/category/pricing reach the PWA via **SCAPI Shopper APIs** (shopper-products v1, shopper-search v1, shopper-promotions v1) proxied through MRT (`/mobify/proxy/api`, shortCode `qmyt7hks`), using `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` v5.2.0 hooks with SLAS private-client auth. OCAPI is a proxied fallback (`/mobify/proxy/ocapi`, dev sandbox `bkzk-002`). MuleSoft does NOT serve product/price to the PWA — its role there is the server-to-server AP21→MuleSoft→SFCC catalogue import (OCAPI Data API or SFTP). Price is separate: AP21→SFCC via pricebook XML import (sfcc-ci / BM Site Import), and per TSD Price (292388871) there is NO direct MuleSoft price integration; mechanism (SFTP/API/MuleSoft) is TBC. Pricebook IDs: `{site}-{currency}-list-prices`/`-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). So SCAPI is fully capable NOW; the real blocker is that SFCC has no catalog/price data yet because that MuleSoft feed isn't built.

**Unblock lower envs:** load catalog + pricebook data into the SFCC sandbox via BM or OCAPI Data API so the PWA can consume via SCAPI immediately. Sample-catalog tooling (`data/sample/catalogs`, `data:import:sample`) is NOT in zimmermann-pwa — it lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo (per Confluence TSD Product page 292061208). The PWA repo only consumes. Confluence coverage checked 2026-07-23 (Mani's "most info is in Confluence" = largely TRUE): BM Config Mgmt (309657601) documents source-controlled `data/core` (catalogue IDs `zimmermann-catalog` + `zimmermann-*-storefront-catalog` now CONFIRMED real; pricebooks/inventory = empty shells, structure only) and sandbox creation via the `zimmermann-sfcc-admin` GitHub Action; loading approach in Catalogue Sync TSDs (312508418 file-based recommended, 315490342 SCAPI Admin API alternative). NB per 315490342: OCAPI is deprecated, admin writes use SCAPI Admin APIs (AmOAuth2), and PRICE has no write API so is ALWAYS file-based (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`). `data/core` auto-imported vs `data/sample` manual demo load per Build&Deploy (264896514). GAP not in Confluence = current runtime state of `bkzk-002` (what is actually loaded now) → that is the Victor part (Victor Crisostomo owns SFCC-121 Validate MuleSoft Sync). These Confluence findings were folded into the deliverable + Confluence draft (page v4) on 2026-07-23: catalogue-ID caveat closed (IDs confirmed), loading mechanism corrected (file-based site-archive import + SCAPI Admin API; OCAPI deprecated; price always file-based), §6 open questions retargeted to Victor's operational items only.

**Permanent vs workaround:** SCAPI-via-MRT (consumption) + MuleSoft catalogue/pricebook feed (population) are permanent. Manual/sample catalog load into sandbox is the temporary workaround. OCAPI fallback is semi-permanent (anything SCAPI doesn't cover).

SCAPI endpoint inventory lives in Section 5.3; the 6 Victor items are carried as Section 2.2 assumptions + Section 7 risks (Owner: Victor). Genre note: this is a spike reframed into a problem/options/decision TSD. Stays DRAFT until the Section 8 Technical Lead sign-off. Independently fact-checked against code + official MRT docs, dash-convention clean. Not yet published to Confluence. Publish target (confirmed by Marcel 2026-07-22): parent page "05.1 — Architecture & Solution Design" (id 277577731, space SFCC), as a sibling of "Technical Solution Design – PWA" (256835585); proposed title "TSD: SFCC MRT API Capabilities (Spike SFCC-122)". URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/349437965. NOT yet linked on the Jira ticket and NOT announced to the squad (draft-only). Note: connector creates a live/current page (no native hidden-draft status), so it IS visible in the tree though clearly marked DRAFT. To finalise later: remove the banner + `[DRAFT]` title prefix + `draft` label, fold in Mani's answers, then link on SFCC-122. Two DoD items remain externally gated: exact sandbox catalogue IDs + data state (need Mani), and "shared with squad" (needs Marcel's publish approval). Note: TSD catalogue IDs (`zimmermann-catalog`, `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`) do NOT match repo sample data (`storefront-catalog-eu`) — confirm with Mani.

Key sources: codebase `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` (SCAPI endpoint inventory §4) and `03-mulesoft.md` (PWA-direct MuleSoft reads: orders/returns/boutique stock only). Happy to guide you through it, Angelo. All three live in the same place: **DevTools → Network tab**. Click a request row, and use the sub-tabs that appear (**Headers**, **Preview**, **Response**). **Preview** gives you a collapsible JSON tree (easiest to read); **Response** is the raw body. If the list looks cleared, just re-navigate the same path with DevTools open.

---

### 1. `product-search` → the `total` field
- **Find it:** type `product-search` in the Network filter box, click the row.
- **Open:** the **Preview** tab.
- **Look for these top-level keys:**
  - `total` — total products matching that category (`cgid`) refinement.
  - `hits` — the array of returned products (up to `limit` = 25); expand it to eyeball real product IDs/names.
- **Interpret:**
  - `total` > 0 (and `hits` has entries) → category is genuinely populated. ✅
  - `total` = 0 / empty `hits` → category empty (unlikely here, since your PDP loaded).

---

### 2. `4673TS251` → the price
- **Find it:** filter `4673TS251`, click the row → **Preview**.
- **Look for:**
  - `currency` → should read `"AUD"`.
  - `price` → the effective price as a number (e.g. `350`).
  - `prices` → an **object keyed by pricebook ID** (because the call used `perPricebook=true`), e.g. `{ "au-aud-list-prices": 350, "au-aud-sale-prices": 280 }`.
- **Interpret:**
  - A real number in `price` **and** `au-aud-*` keys in `prices` → the **pricebook is loaded *and* assigned to the site** (the strongest proof — not just the product). ✅
  - `price` is `null`/`0` or `prices` is missing/empty → product exists but the **pricebook isn't loaded/assigned** (that would be a real gap to flag).
- **Bonus (free, since the call also has `expand=availability`):** look for `inventory` → `ats` / `orderable`. The BM docs said inventory lists ship as *empty shells*, so don't be surprised if stock is absent — that's expected and separate from pricing.

---

### 3. The `59b4364e-...` 404
- **Find it:** filter `59b4364e`, click the row.
- **Open the Headers tab first** and read the **Request URL** (full path). The path segment *just before* the UUID names the resource. Also note the **domain**:
  - `api.cquotient.com` or path has `einstein` / `recommendations` → **Einstein recommender** not configured → benign (matches the TSD's static-fallback note).
  - `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` with `.../baskets/{uuid}` → a **stale basket** the app tried to restore, then re-created (you can see a fresh `baskets` 200 right after) → benign.
  - `.../customers/{uuid}` or `.../product-lists/{uuid}` → a **guest resource that doesn't exist yet** → benign.
- **Then the Preview/Response tab** shows the error body (`title` / `type` / `detail`) which usually names exactly what wasn't found.
- **Interpret:** if it's any of the three above, it's noise for a fresh guest session and nothing you depend on. If the path points at something the page actually renders (content/config), that's worth a flag.

---

**Fastest way to close this out:** paste back three things and I'll confirm and bake the exact values straight into the TSD (§2.2 confirmed, §7 resolved-for-dev, §6 smoke-test result, §8 decision-record line):
1. the `total` number from #1,

SFCC-122 "Spike: Document SFCC MRT API Capabilities" — Jira Spike, project SFCC (zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net), label Squad-A, High, **In Progress**, assigned to Marcel, reported by Jasmijn Tsang. Sibling spikes: SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync, Victor Crisostomo, Ready for Dev), SFCC-123 (Contentful design, Jhoan Rose, In Progress). Board spike house style: Objective / Background / Tasks / Definition of Done (see [[f2r-spike]]).

Objective: document the MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs available for product, category, and pricing so the squad knows what can be built/tested in lower environments while MuleSoft is not yet ready. Background note: "Angelo (=Marcel) to set up session with Mani." Mani = Manikandan Ramachandran (owns SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments epic).

**Crux finding (the reframe the spike needs):** MRT is primarily the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer. IMPORTANT correction (per official MRT docs, audited 2026-07-22): there IS a real "Managed Runtime API" but it is an ADMIN/deployment REST API (mrt-admin: environments/targets, bundles, deploy, redirects, proxies, env vars, CDN invalidation, access-control headers, certs, users), NOT a commerce-data API. The deliverable's original flat claim "MRT is not an API" was WRONG; corrected via audit fixes B1-B4 (applied 2026-07-23, doc + Confluence page now v3). Accurate framing now in the doc (3.1.0, 3.1.9): the MRT Admin API = platform admin/CI-CD (out of scope for this spike), while product/category/pricing data comes via SCAPI reached through the MRT proxy (/mobify/proxy/api). Audit also added an MRT platform capabilities/constraints table (render timeout 20s/16s, 6MB req/resp, cookies-off-by-default/allow_cookies, bundle limits, reserved /mobify prefix, built-in env vars, edge services, ap-southeast-2 region). Product/category/pricing reach the PWA via **SCAPI Shopper APIs** (shopper-products v1, shopper-search v1, shopper-promotions v1) proxied through MRT (`/mobify/proxy/api`, shortCode `qmyt7hks`), using `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` v5.2.0 hooks with SLAS private-client auth. OCAPI is a proxied fallback (`/mobify/proxy/ocapi`, dev sandbox `bkzk-002`). MuleSoft does NOT serve product/price to the PWA — its role there is the server-to-server AP21→MuleSoft→SFCC catalogue import (OCAPI Data API or SFTP). Price is separate: AP21→SFCC via pricebook XML import (sfcc-ci / BM Site Import), and per TSD Price (292388871) there is NO direct MuleSoft price integration; mechanism (SFTP/API/MuleSoft) is TBC. Pricebook IDs: `{site}-{currency}-list-prices`/`-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). So SCAPI is fully capable NOW; the real blocker is that SFCC has no catalog/price data yet because that MuleSoft feed isn't built.

**Unblock lower envs:** load catalog + pricebook data into the SFCC sandbox via BM or OCAPI Data API so the PWA can consume via SCAPI immediately. Sample-catalog tooling (`data/sample/catalogs`, `data:import:sample`) is NOT in zimmermann-pwa — it lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo (per Confluence TSD Product page 292061208). The PWA repo only consumes. Confluence coverage checked 2026-07-23 (Mani's "most info is in Confluence" = largely TRUE): BM Config Mgmt (309657601) documents source-controlled `data/core` (catalogue IDs `zimmermann-catalog` + `zimmermann-*-storefront-catalog` now CONFIRMED real; pricebooks/inventory = empty shells, structure only) and sandbox creation via the `zimmermann-sfcc-admin` GitHub Action; loading approach in Catalogue Sync TSDs (312508418 file-based recommended, 315490342 SCAPI Admin API alternative). NB per 315490342: OCAPI is deprecated, admin writes use SCAPI Admin APIs (AmOAuth2), and PRICE has no write API so is ALWAYS file-based (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`). `data/core` auto-imported vs `data/sample` manual demo load per Build&Deploy (264896514). GAP not in Confluence = current runtime state of `bkzk-002` (what is actually loaded now) → that is the Victor part (Victor Crisostomo owns SFCC-121 Validate MuleSoft Sync). UPDATE 2026-07-23: Angelo ran the PWA locally against dev and captured the network calls. Dev `bkzk-002` IS populated: categories (`clothing` levels=2, `new-arrivals`) returned 200; `product-search` with `cgid` returned 200 (~3.3 kB); and the PDP `shopper-products` call for master `4673TS251` (the TSD's own example style) returned 200 (~3.5 kB) with `expand=prices/promotions/availability`, `currency=AUD`. So the "empty data" premise does NOT hold for dev, the sample/seed catalogue appears already loaded, and open item #1 is largely answered for dev. Still open: exact search hit count/data completeness, other sites/tiers, permanent feed timeline, and one repeated 404 on a UUID resource (`59b4364e-...`) likely an Einstein recommender or not-yet-created guest resource (benign, to confirm). These Confluence findings were folded into the deliverable + Confluence draft (page v4) on 2026-07-23: catalogue-ID caveat closed (IDs confirmed), loading mechanism corrected (file-based site-archive import + SCAPI Admin API; OCAPI deprecated; price always file-based), §6 open questions retargeted to Victor's operational items only.

**Permanent vs workaround:** SCAPI-via-MRT (consumption) + MuleSoft catalogue/pricebook feed (population) are permanent. Manual/sample catalog load into sandbox is the temporary workaround. OCAPI fallback is semi-permanent (anything SCAPI doesn't cover).

content.text:
All three confirmed. Here's what you're looking at, explained.

## 1. `product-search` — the search-result envelope

SCAPI's `shopper-search` returns a **result set**, not products directly. The fields that matter:

- **`total: 1`** — this is the headline. It's the count of products matching your filter (`selectedRefinements: {cgid: "clothing"}`), across the *whole* result, not just this page. So the **clothing category currently contains exactly one master style**.
- **`limit: 1` / `offset: 0`** — pagination. This call asked for 1 item starting at 0. (`total` is independent of `limit` — even if you'd asked for 25, `total` would still be 1.)
- **`hits: [...]`** — the actual products returned. Each hit carries `productId`, `productName`, `price`, `priceRanges`, `image`, `variants`, `variationAttributes`.

**What it means:** category browsing works, and dev is populated — but with a **thin seed**: one fully-built style (`4673TS251` "Illuminate Fitted Blouse"). That's plenty to wire up and test components, PDP, PLP, and cart, but *not* enough to test pagination, faceting at scale, or category breadth. That's the important refinement to our earlier "it's populated" conclusion.

## 2. `4673TS251` — the product record

This is the `shopper-products` getProduct response. What each key proves:

- **`currency: "AUD"` + `price: 625`** — a real price came back.
- **`priceRanges: [{ minPrice: 625, maxPrice: 625, pricebook: "au-aud-list-prices" }]`** — this is the strongest single proof. - **Off-scope (cart/account):** `baskets`, `product-lists`. These are checkout and wishlist/account territory — not product/category/pricing. They prove the *broader* SCAPI surface is alive, but they aren't what the spike is about.
- **Anomaly to explain, not evidence:** `shopper-context` 404 — an edge case, belongs in §5.4, not §6.
- **Unknown:** `configurations` — can't be scoped until identified.

|---|---|---|

Jamming `baskets` and `product-lists` into the core verification would pad §6 with out-of-scope signals and blur what the spike proved. The disciplined move is **scope-aligned**, not "use everything":

Applying "one TSD = one problem" strictly, here's the verdict.

## The one problem
*"Can the storefront consume **product, category, and pricing** data in the lower environments before MuleSoft, and how?"* Anything not serving that is a different problem, hence a different TSD.

## Verdict: which APIs are part of *this* TSD

**IN — they serve the one problem (product / category / pricing):**

| API | Why it's in |
|---|---|
| **Shopper Products** (`getProduct`) | Product data + pricing (`priceRanges` → pricebook) |
| **Shopper Search** (`productSearch`) | Category listing (`cgid`) + search |
| **Shopper Products `getCategory`** (`clothing`, `new-arrivals`) | The category tree itself |
| **Shopper Promotions** | Pricing/promotions (part of "pricing") |
| **SLAS / Shopper Login** | The auth **enabler** — you can't read any of the above without it. In scope as the access mechanism, not as a subject in its own right |

**OUT — each belongs to its own problem / TSD:**

| API (observed call) | Different problem it belongs to |
|---|---|
| **Shopper Baskets** (`baskets`) | Cart / checkout |
| **Shopper Customers – product-lists** (`product-lists`) | Account / wishlist |
| **Shopper Context** (the `59b4364e` 404) | Personalization / segmentation |
| **`configurations`** (+ Einstein / Data Cloud) | Personalization / analytics / platform bootstrap |
| **Shopper Orders** | Checkout / order placement (and order *history* is MuleSoft, already noted as out) |

## What this means for the current TSD (a real tightening)
Two consequences, and one of them fixes an over-scope I introduced:

1. **§5.3 currently over-scopes.** Its interface table lists **seven** shopper families — including Baskets, Orders, and Customers. Under the one-problem rule, those three don't belong here. **Trim §5.3 to the four in-scope APIs** (Products, Search, Promotions, SLAS). The others get at most a single "documented separately" pointer, not a table row.
2. **The earlier "use all the calls" debate is settled the strict way: no.** Only categories + search + product (+ SLAS auth) are evidence in §6. `baskets`/`product-lists` are **not even a footnote** here — they're a different problem. And I should **not** add the `shopper-context` 404 to §5.4 as I proposed — that would be importing a personalization concern into a product/pricing TSD. It stays a diagnostic note in *our* conversation, not in the doc.

So the clean answer: **this TSD is about four APIs** — Shopper Products, Shopper Search, Shopper Products/getCategory, Shopper Promotions — gated by **SLAS**. Everything else you saw in the network trace is real and healthy, but it's evidence for *other* TSDs, not this one.

## Net effect on the doc
- **§5.3:** trim 7 → 4 (+ a one-line "cart, account, personalization APIs are out of scope, see their own TSDs").
- **§6:** evidence = categories/search/product/auth only.
- **§5.4:** drop the shopper-context idea.
- **§2.2 / §7 / §8:** the dev-verification updates still apply (they're about the in-scope product/category/pricing data).

Want me to apply this tightened, scope-pure version to the Confluence page (trim §5.3, scope §6, plus the v0.3 verification updates)? And still your call on the `configurations` URL — though by this verdict it's out of scope regardless, so we can simply leave it out.

1. Problem Statement
--------------------

### 1.1 Context

The Zimmermann storefront is a PWA Kit application on Managed Runtime (MRT) that consumes commerce data from SFCC. Building and testing the storefront (product listing, product detail, pricing) in the lower environments requires product, category, and pricing data to be available through the APIs the storefront calls.

### 1.2 Problem

Product and price data are absent from the lower environments because the source-to-SFCC feeds are not built yet (catalogue: AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC; price: AP21 to SFCC). Compounding this, "SFCC MRT API capabilities" is ambiguous across the squad: it is unclear what Managed Runtime itself provides versus what the storefront consumes. Without a clear, documented picture of the available APIs and a way to populate data, front-end build and test are blocked.

### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved

Squad-A cannot build or test product listing, product detail, or pricing against real data. Work either stalls or proceeds against mocks that drift from the real SCAPI responses, creating rework and schedule risk, while the team waits on the MuleSoft integration (SFCC-121) with no interim path.

### 1.4 Success Criteria

* A documented inventory of the SFCC APIs available through MRT for product, category, and pricing (endpoints, authentication, payload).
* A confirmed, repeatable way to populate the `bkzk-002` sandbox so `shopper-products`, `shopper-search`, and pricing return data.
* Front-end can consume product, category, and price via SCAPI in a lower environment with no code change once data exists.
* A clear separation of permanent architecture versus interim workaround.

---

2. Constraints & Assumptions
----------------------------

### 2.1 Constraints

| Constraint | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. |
| Integration layer | Catalogue, price, order, and stock data reach SFCC through MuleSoft or server-side feeds. The PWA does not call AP21 or other back-office systems directly. |
| Data consumption | The storefront reads commerce data only via SCAPI Shopper APIs through the MRT proxy; it does not write catalogue or price data. |
| Storefront scope | Must work across all Zimmermann storefronts (10 PWA sites over 7 SFCC sites). No single-market workaround. |

### 2.2 Assumptions

| Assumption | Risk if Wrong |
| --- | --- |
| SCAPI can serve product, category, and pricing once data exists (verified against the codebase). | If wrong, the block is an API gap, not just data. Verified, so low risk. |
| The `bkzk-002` sandbox can be populated now via a `data/core` import plus a manual sample-data load, independent of MuleSoft. | If wrong (no sample data, or no access), the interim unblock fails and the team must wait for the MuleSoft feed. To confirm with Victor. |
| First-time BM setup (storefront-catalogue assignment, search-index rebuild) can be completed on the sandbox. | If incomplete, `shopper-search` returns nothing even with a catalogue loaded. To confirm with Victor. |
| Front-end has, or can obtain, access to run the load, or platform runs it on request. | If wrong, the team cannot self-serve the interim load. To confirm with Victor. |

---

3. Options Analysis
-------------------

The sub-problem: how do we get product, category, and price data into the lower environments so the squad can build now, before the MuleSoft feed exists?

**Sources.** Options A and B, and the preference for A over B, are taken from Confluence "TSD: Catalogue Sync, SCAPI Admin API Design (Alternative Pattern)" (315490342) and its parent file-based design (312508418), which name file-based import as the recommended approach for Zimmermann's catalogue scale and the SCAPI Admin API as the alternative. Those pages describe the permanent MuleSoft to SFCC sync; the same mechanisms are applied here to the interim sample load (see Section 4.2). Option C is the status-quo baseline, included for completeness and not drawn from a source document.

### 3.1 Options Summary

| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Option A: File-based import** (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`) of the `data/core` structure plus `data/sample` data | + Recommended by Confluence for catalogue scale + Single repeatable bulk load; handles sequencing + Only pattern that also loads price (pricebook XML) | - Needs sandbox/WebDAV access and someone to run it - Sample data is not production-representative | Yes |
| **Option B: SCAPI Admin API** per record (Products + Inventory Lists, AmOAuth2) | + Real-time per product; no file staging | - Thousands of calls for bulk; rate-limited; caller must enforce sequencing - No pricebook write API, so price still needs file-based | Supplementary only |
| **Option C: Wait for the MuleSoft feed** (no interim load) | + No interim throwaway work | - Blocks front-end build/test until SFCC-121 lands; timeline unknown | No |

### 3.2 Option Detail

#### Option A: File-based import

Apply the source-controlled structure (`npm run data:import:core` / `sfcc-ci instance:import`), then load a filtered sample catalogue from `data/sample/` and pricebook XML via WebDAV plus the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job. This is Confluence's recommended pattern for Zimmermann's catalogue scale and is the only pattern that can load price data. Source: Confluence 315490342 (Context callout and Section 9) and 312508418.

#### Option B: SCAPI Admin API (supplementary)

MuleSoft (or a script) calls the SCAPI Products and Inventory Lists Admin APIs per record, authenticated via Account Manager OAuth2. Suited to real-time single-product updates, not bulk load, and it cannot write pricebooks. Useful later for deltas; not the interim unblock. Source: Confluence 315490342 (Sections 4, 6, and 9).

#### Option C: Wait for MuleSoft *(Discarded)*

Discarded: it leaves the front-end blocked for an unknown period (dependency on SFCC-121) when an interim load is available. Baseline option; no source document.

4. Recommended Option & Rationale
---------------------------------

### 4.1 Recommended Option

**Option A: File-based import of the** `data/core` **structure plus** `data/sample` **sample data.**

### 4.2 Rationale

Option A matches the Confluence-recommended pattern for catalogue scale (per "TSD: Catalogue Sync", 315490342 Section 9 and its parent 312508418), is a single repeatable load, and is the only option that also populates price (per 315490342 Section 5: no pricebook write API exists). It unblocks front-end build and test with no code change and is independent of the MuleSoft feed timeline. Option B is retained only as a supplementary, real-time mechanism; Option C blocks the squad.

Note: the Confluence recommendation is written for the permanent MuleSoft to SFCC sync. The same load mechanism (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`) applies here to the interim sample load, so the recommendation carries over; framing it as the interim unblock is this TSD's extension, not a verbatim Confluence recommendation.

### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted

The interim sample load is throwaway once the permanent AP21-to-MuleSoft-to-SFCC feed is delivering. It depends on sandbox/WebDAV access and someone running the import (a dependency on platform / Victor), and the sample data is not production-representative.

---

5. Technical Implementation
---------------------------

### 5.1 High-Level Sequence

1. Apply the source-controlled structure: `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) loads the catalogues (`zimmermann-catalog`, `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`) and the empty pricebook and inventory shells. Safe to re-run.
2. Load sample product data: import the filtered sample catalogue from `data/sample/` (manual, for dev and demo).
3. Load sample prices: deliver Pricebook XML via WebDAV and run the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job. IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices`.
4. Complete first-time BM setup: storefront-catalogue assignment per site, pricebook assignment, and a search-index rebuild.
5. Verify: obtain a SLAS guest token and run a `shopper-search` call for a known category. If it returns zero results, rebuild the search index (step 4) and retry.
6. Front-end consumes product, category, and price via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No code change is required.

### 5.2 Component / API Changes

| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sfccworkplace` `data/core` import | Apply catalogues + pricebook/inventory shells to the sandbox | Config (existing tooling) |
| `sfccworkplace` `data/sample` import | Manually load sample products for dev/demo | Config |
| Pricebook XML via WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import` | Load sample prices | Config |
| Business Manager first-time setup | Catalogue assignment, pricebook assignment, search-index rebuild | Config |
| PWA `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks | None; the storefront already consumes SCAPI | No change |

### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces

The storefront consumes SCAPI Shopper APIs through the MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api` (`config/default.js:131`), base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (Dev: `qmyt7hks...`), SLAS private-client auth. Params: `clientId`, `organizationId` (`f_ecom_bkzk_002`), `shortCode` (`qmyt7hks`), `siteId` (`ZimmermannAU` default).

| API family | Path root | Serves | Verbs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail, master/variant, images, prices | GET |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category listing (`cgid`), search, faceting, sort | GET |
| Shopper Promotions | `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | Active promotions, coupon validation | GET |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | Guest and registered auth, token lifecycle | GET, POST |
| Shopper Baskets | `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*` | Basket / cart lifecycle | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE |
| Shopper Orders | `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*` | Placement and lookup of the just-placed order (order history is via MuleSoft) | POST, GET |
| Shopper Customers | `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references | GET, POST, PATCH |

Canonical product/category/pricing query (proven in `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:52-58`):

`useProductSearch({
parameters: {
refine: ["cgid=<categoryId>", "htype=master"],
expand: ["promotions", "variations", "prices", "images", "custom_properties"],
perPricebook: true,
allVariationProperties: true
}
})`

Out of scope for this problem, documented for completeness: OCAPI via `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` (configured, not called from app code); MuleSoft direct reads via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft` (orders, returns, boutique stock only, not yet wired); Einstein recommendations; and the Managed Runtime Admin API (`mrt-admin`), which administers environments, bundles, and proxies and is platform / CI-CD, not commerce data.

### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shopper-search` returns zero results after a catalogue load | Search index not rebuilt; rebuild it in BM, then results appear | Edge case |
| Prices do not render on PDP/PLP | Pricebook not loaded or not assigned to the site; load pricebook XML and assign | Edge case |
| SLAS guest token / session fails on MRT | Server-Side Cookie Access (`allow_cookies`) is off on the environment; enable it | Error |
| SCAPI 5xx on catalogue read | `commerce-sdk-react` retries with backoff; show cached data or an error state | Error |

### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes

* **Commerce API params:** `config/default.js:130-138` (env-injected). **Proxies:** `config/default.js:208-217` (`api` to SCAPI, `ocapi` to sandbox). **SLAS private client:** `overrides/app/ssr.js:52`.
* **Per-environment config:** `config/{dev,test,sit,staging,uat,production}.js`; switch with `npm run env -- <tier>`; deploy with `npm run push:<tier>` (`pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`). MRT environment variables are managed in the Runtime Admin console / Admin API and rotated independently of the codebase.
* **MRT platform constraints** (official docs): render timeout 20s prod / 16s non-prod; request/response 6 MB; cookies off by default (enable `allow_cookies`); reserved `/mobify` path prefix; `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney) is a supported region.
* **Current sandbox configuration state is unconfirmed** (whether structure and data are loaded, and whether BM first-time setup is complete); this is an open item for Victor (Section 7).

---

6. Testing & Validation
-----------------------

### 6.1 Test Coverage

| Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Integration | SCAPI reachability from the sandbox (SLAS guest token to `shopper-search`) | Returns more than zero products for a known `cgid` |
| Integration | Pricing via `expand=prices`, `perPricebook=true` | Product returns list and sale price from the assigned pricebook |
| E2E / Playwright (@p0) | PLP and PDP render against sandbox data | Category page lists products; PDP shows price and images |
| Unit | `commerce-sdk-react` hooks consume the responses | Hooks return typed product / search results |

### 6.2 Regression Risk

Low. This work loads data into a lower-environment sandbox and documents the consumption path; it changes no production application code. The PWA already consumes SCAPI, so populating data does not alter app logic. Guard: ensure sample data is not promoted to higher environments.

---

7. Risks & Mitigations
----------------------

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current `bkzk-002` data state unknown; may be empty | Med | Confirm with Victor; run `data:import:core` + sample load if needed | Victor (SFCC-121) |
| No usable sample dataset, or no access to run the load | Med | Confirm sample data exists; obtain sandbox / WebDAV / `sfcc-ci` access | Victor / Platform |

| MuleSoft catalogue/price feed timeline unknown (SFCC-121) | High | Interim sample load carries build and test until the feed lands | Victor (SFCC-121) |
| Cookies off by default on MRT breaks the SLAS refresh flow | Low | Enable Server-Side Cookie Access (`allow_cookies`) per environment | Platform |
| MuleSoft real-time rate limits unconfirmed (direct-read path) | Low | Not needed for product/price; confirm before wiring order/stock reads | Integration Lead |

Not approved for implementation until the Section 8 sign-off is completed by the Technical Lead. ## Document Information | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Document ID** | TSD-SFCC-122 | | **Author(s)** | Angelo Navarro, Squad-A / FED Lead | | **Reviewer(s)** | Technical Lead (to be confirmed) | | **Created** | 22 Jul 2026 | | **Version** | v0.3, Draft | | **Status** | Draft | | **Related Jira** | SFCC-122 | --- ## Version History | Version | Date | Summary of Change | Author | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | v0.1 | 22 Jul 2026 | Initial spike inventory (pre-template): SCAPI-via-MRT capabilities for product, category, pricing | Angelo Navarro | | v0.2 | 23 Jul 2026 | Restructured into the TSD template; folded in verified Confluence findings; "MRT API" scope clarified (Admin API vs SCAPI); source citations added to Sections 3 and 4 | Angelo Navarro | | v0.3 | 24 Jul 2026 | Folded in dev-sandbox verification (populated, single-product seed) and Victor's confirmations; tightened scope to the product/category/pricing APIs (Baskets/Orders/Customers moved out per one-problem); updated assumptions, risks, and decision record | Angelo Navarro | --- ## 1. Problem Statement ### 1.1 Context The Zimmermann storefront is a PWA Kit application on Managed Runtime (MRT) that consumes commerce data from SFCC. Building and testing the storefront (product listing, product detail, pricing) in the lower environments requires product, category, and pricing data to be available through the APIs the storefront calls. ### 1.2 Problem Product and price data are absent from the lower environments because the source-to-SFCC feeds are not built yet (catalogue: AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC; price: AP21 to SFCC). Compounding this, "SFCC MRT API capabilities" is ambiguous across the squad: it is unclear what Managed Runtime itself provides versus what the storefront consumes. Without a clear, documented picture of the available APIs and a way to populate data, front-end build and test are blocked. ### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved Squad-A cannot build or test product listing, product detail, or pricing against real data. Work either stalls or proceeds against mocks that drift from the real SCAPI responses, creating rework and schedule risk, while the team waits on the MuleSoft integration (SFCC-121) with no interim path. ### 1.4 Success Criteria * A documented inventory of the SFCC APIs available through MRT for product, category, and pricing (endpoints, authentication, payload). * A confirmed, repeatable way to populate the `bkzk-002` sandbox so `shopper-products`, `shopper-search`, and pricing return data. * Front-end can consume product, category, and price via SCAPI in a lower environment with no code change once data exists. * A clear separation of permanent architecture versus interim workaround. *(Status: the success criteria are now largely met for dev, see Sections 6 and 8.)* --- ## 2. Constraints & Assumptions ### 2.1 Constraints | Constraint | Detail | | --- | --- | | Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. | | Integration layer | Catalogue, price, order, and stock data reach SFCC through MuleSoft or server-side feeds. The PWA does not call AP21 or other back-office systems directly. | | Data consumption | The storefront reads commerce data only via SCAPI Shopper APIs through the MRT proxy; it does not write catalogue or price data. | | Storefront scope | Must work across all Zimmermann storefronts (10 PWA sites over 7 SFCC sites). No single-market workaround. | ### 2.2 Assumptions | Assumption | Status / Risk if Wrong | | --- | --- | | SCAPI can serve product, category, and pricing once data exists. | **Confirmed** (24 Jul, local run): categories, `product-search`, and product all returned 200 with real data. | | The `bkzk-002` sandbox can be populated for the interim, independent of MuleSoft. | **Confirmed** (Victor + local run): categories, pricebooks, and inventory are configured, with one sample product priced and stocked. Residual: it is a single-product seed; breadth and other sites/tiers are unconfirmed. | | First-time BM setup (storefront-catalogue assignment, search-index rebuild) is complete on the sandbox. | **Confirmed** (Victor: done as part of developer setup; local `shopper-search` returns results). | | Front-end has, or can obtain, access to load data. | **Partial:** platform performed the dev setup; SCAPI credentials for the write/Admin path are to be provided (Victor). Consumption uses SLAS, which already works. | --- ## 3. Options Analysis The sub-problem: how do we get product, category, and price data into the lower environments so the squad can build now, before the MuleSoft feed exists? **Sources.** Options A and B, and the preference for A over B, are taken from Confluence "TSD: Catalogue Sync, SCAPI Admin API Design (Alternative Pattern)" (315490342) and its parent file-based design (312508418), which name file-based import as the recommended approach for Zimmermann's catalogue scale and the SCAPI Admin API as the alternative. Those pages describe the permanent MuleSoft to SFCC sync; the same mechanisms are applied here to the interim sample load (see Section 4.2). Option C is the status-quo baseline, included for completeness and not drawn from a source document. ### 3.1 Options Summary | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Option A: File-based import** (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`) of the `data/core` structure plus `data/sample` data | + Recommended by Confluence for catalogue scale
+ Single repeatable bulk load; handles sequencing
+ Only pattern that also loads price (pricebook XML) | - Needs sandbox/WebDAV access and someone to run it
- Sample data is not production-representative | Yes | | **Option B: SCAPI Admin API** per record (Products + Inventory Lists, AmOAuth2) | + Real-time per product; no file staging | - Thousands of calls for bulk; rate-limited; caller must enforce sequencing
- No pricebook write API, so price still needs file-based | Supplementary only | | **Option C: Wait for the MuleSoft feed** (no interim load) | + No interim throwaway work | - Blocks front-end build/test until SFCC-121 lands; timeline unknown | No | ### 3.2 Option Detail #### Option A: File-based import Apply the source-controlled structure (`npm run data:import:core` / `sfcc-ci instance:import`), then load a filtered sample catalogue from `data/sample/` and pricebook XML via WebDAV plus the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job. This is Confluence's recommended pattern for Zimmermann's catalogue scale and is the only pattern that can load price data. Source: Confluence 315490342 (Context callout and Section 9) and 312508418. #### Option B: SCAPI Admin API (supplementary) MuleSoft (or a script) calls the SCAPI Products and Inventory Lists Admin APIs per record, authenticated via Account Manager OAuth2. Suited to real-time single-product updates, not bulk load, and it cannot write pricebooks. Useful later for deltas; not the interim unblock. Source: Confluence 315490342 (Sections 4, 6, and 9). #### Option C: Wait for MuleSoft *(Discarded)* Discarded: it leaves the front-end blocked for an unknown period (dependency on SFCC-121) when an interim load is available. Baseline option; no source document. --- ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale ### 4.1 Recommended Option **Option A: File-based import of the `data/core` structure plus `data/sample` sample data.** ### 4.2 Rationale Option A matches the Confluence-recommended pattern for catalogue scale (per "TSD: Catalogue Sync", 315490342 Section 9 and its parent 312508418), is a single repeatable load, and is the only option that also populates price (per 315490342 Section 5: no pricebook write API exists). It unblocks front-end build and test with no code change and is independent of the MuleSoft feed timeline. Option B is retained only as a supplementary, real-time mechanism; Option C blocks the squad. Note: the Confluence recommendation is written for the permanent MuleSoft to SFCC sync. The same load mechanism (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`) applies here to the interim sample load, so the recommendation carries over; framing it as the interim unblock is this TSD's extension, not a verbatim Confluence recommendation. ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted The interim sample load is throwaway once the permanent AP21-to-MuleSoft-to-SFCC feed is delivering. It depends on sandbox/WebDAV access and someone running the import (a dependency on platform / Victor), and the sample data is not production-representative. **Status (24 Jul):** for dev, this interim load is already in place, one sample product with an AU list price and inventory (confirmed by Victor and verified via local run). The recommendation now applies to broadening the sample set and extending to other sites and tiers, not to a first load. --- ## 5. Technical Implementation ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence 1. Apply the source-controlled structure: `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) loads the catalogues (`zimmermann-catalog`, `zimmermann--storefront-catalog`) and the empty pricebook and inventory shells. Safe to re-run. 2. Load sample product data: import the filtered sample catalogue from `data/sample/` (manual, for dev and demo). 3. Load sample prices: deliver Pricebook XML via WebDAV and run the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job. IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices`. 4. Complete first-time BM setup: storefront-catalogue assignment per site, pricebook assignment, and a search-index rebuild. 5. Verify: obtain a SLAS guest token and run a `shopper-search` call for a known category. If it returns zero results, rebuild the search index (step 4) and retry. 6. Front-end consumes product, category, and price via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No code change is required. (For dev, steps 1 to 4 have already been performed by platform as part of developer setup; step 5 is verified, see Section 6.) ### 5.2 Component / API Changes | File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | `sfccworkplace` `data/core` import | Apply catalogues + pricebook/inventory shells to the sandbox | Config (existing tooling) | | `sfccworkplace` `data/sample` import | Manually load sample products for dev/demo | Config | | Pricebook XML via WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import` | Load sample prices | Config | | Business Manager first-time setup | Catalogue assignment, pricebook assignment, search-index rebuild | Config | | PWA `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks | None; the storefront already consumes SCAPI | No change | ### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces The storefront consumes SCAPI Shopper APIs through the MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api` (`config/default.js:131`), base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (Dev: `qmyt7hks...`), SLAS private-client auth. Scoped to this TSD's one problem (product, category, pricing consumption): | API family | Path root | Serves | Verbs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` (products and `categories/{id}`) | Product detail, master/variant, images, prices; and the category tree | GET | | Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid`), search, faceting, sort | GET | | Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | Guest and registered auth; the access enabler for the calls above | GET, POST | Promotion and price data are surfaced via `expand=promotions,prices` (per-pricebook) on the Products and Search calls above; the storefront does not call a standalone Shopper Promotions endpoint for browsing (coupon validation is a checkout concern, out of scope here). Canonical product/category/pricing query (proven in `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:52-58`): ```js useProductSearch({ parameters: { refine: ["cgid=", "htype=master"], expand: ["promotions", "variations", "prices", "images", "custom_properties"], perPricebook: true, allVariationProperties: true } }) ``` **Out of scope for this TSD** (one problem = product/category/pricing consumption). Each is its own concern or TSD and is listed only so the boundary is explicit: - **Shopper Baskets** (cart/checkout; used in the app via `useCurrentBasket`). - **Shopper Orders** (checkout / order placement; order history comes from MuleSoft). - **Shopper Customers** (account, addresses, wishlist / product-lists). - **Shopper Context** (personalization/segmentation; a `GET` 404 for a fresh guest is expected). - **Einstein and Data Cloud** (recommendations, analytics). - **Managed Runtime Admin API** (`mrt-admin`): environments, bundles, proxies; platform and CI-CD. - **OCAPI** via `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` (configured, not called from app code) and **MuleSoft direct reads** via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft` (not yet wired). ### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases | Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type | | --- | --- | --- | | `shopper-search` returns zero results after a catalogue load | Search index not rebuilt; rebuild it in BM, then results appear | Edge case | | Prices do not render on PDP/PLP | Pricebook not loaded or not assigned to the site; load pricebook XML and assign | Edge case | | SLAS guest token / session fails on MRT | Server-Side Cookie Access (`allow_cookies`) is off on the environment; enable it | Error | | SCAPI 5xx on catalogue read | `commerce-sdk-react` retries with backoff; show cached data or an error state | Error | ### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes * **Commerce API params:** `config/default.js:130-138` (env-injected). **Proxies:** `config/default.js:208-217` (`api` to SCAPI, `ocapi` to sandbox). **SLAS private client:** `overrides/app/ssr.js:52`. * **Per-environment config:** `config/{dev,test,sit,staging,uat,production}.js`; switch with `npm run env -- `; deploy with `npm run push:` (`pwa-kit-dev push -t `). MRT environment variables are managed in the Runtime Admin console / Admin API and rotated independently of the codebase. * **MRT platform constraints** (official docs): render timeout 20s prod / 16s non-prod; request/response 6 MB; cookies off by default (enable `allow_cookies`); reserved `/mobify` path prefix; `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney) is a supported region. * **Current sandbox state (confirmed 24 Jul):** dev `bkzk-002` is configured with categories, pricebooks, and inventory, plus one sample product (`4673TS251`) priced in AUD (`au-aud-list-prices`) and stocked (`inventory_m_au`, ats 10). Confirmed by Victor and verified via local run. Breadth (single product), other sites, and other tiers remain unconfirmed. SCAPI credentials for the write/Admin path are to be provided. --- ## 6. Testing & Validation ### 6.1 Test Coverage | Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria | | --- | --- | --- | | Integration | SCAPI reachability from the sandbox (SLAS guest token to `shopper-search`) | Returns more than zero products for a known `cgid` | | Integration | Pricing via `expand=prices`, `perPricebook=true` | Product returns list and sale price from the assigned pricebook | | E2E / Playwright (@p0) | PLP and PDP render against sandbox data | Category page lists products; PDP shows price and images | | Unit | `commerce-sdk-react` hooks consume the responses | Hooks return typed product / search results | ### 6.2 Regression Risk Low. This work loads data into a lower-environment sandbox and documents the consumption path; it changes no production application code. The PWA already consumes SCAPI, so populating data does not alter app logic. Guard: ensure sample data is not promoted to higher environments. ### 6.3 Verification Performed (dev, 24 Jul 2026) A local PWA run against dev `bkzk-002` (homepage to category to PDP) confirmed the in-scope consumption path end to end: * **SLAS guest auth:** working (guest token issued; `baskets` and `product-lists` 200 as a side effect). * **Category tree:** `categories/clothing` (levels=2) and `categories/new-arrivals` returned 200 (navigable). * **Search:** `product-search` with `refine=cgid=clothing` returned 200 with `total: 1`. * **Product and pricing:** `products/4673TS251` returned 200 with `price: 625`, `currency: AUD`, sourced from pricebook `au-aud-list-prices`, and `inventory_m_au` `ats: 10`, `orderable: true`, plus the full variant and attribute set. Consumption uses SLAS, which already works. | --- ## 3. Options Analysis The sub-problem: how do we get product, category, and price data into the lower environments so the squad can build now, before the MuleSoft feed exists? **Sources.** Options A and B, and the preference for A over B, are taken from Confluence "TSD: Catalogue Sync, SCAPI Admin API Design (Alternative Pattern)" (315490342) and its parent file-based design (312508418), which name file-based import as the recommended approach for Zimmermann's catalogue scale and the SCAPI Admin API as the alternative. Those pages describe the permanent MuleSoft to SFCC sync; the same mechanisms are applied here to the interim sample load (see Section 4.2). Option C is the status-quo baseline, included for completeness and not drawn from a source document. ### 3.1 Options Summary | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Option A: File-based import** (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`) of the `data/core` structure plus `data/sample` data | + Recommended by Confluence for catalogue scale
+ Single repeatable bulk load; handles sequencing
+ Only pattern that also loads price (pricebook XML) | - Needs sandbox/WebDAV access and someone to run it
- Sample data is not production-representative | Yes | | **Option B: SCAPI Admin API** per record (Products + Inventory Lists, AmOAuth2) | + Real-time per product; no file staging | - Thousands of calls for bulk; rate-limited; caller must enforce sequencing
- No pricebook write API, so price still needs file-based | Supplementary only | | **Option C: Wait for the MuleSoft feed** (no interim load) | + No interim throwaway work | - Blocks front-end build/test until SFCC-121 lands; timeline unknown | No | ### 3.2 Option Detail #### Option A: File-based import Apply the source-controlled structure (`npm run data:import:core` / `sfcc-ci instance:import`), then load a filtered sample catalogue from `data/sample/` and pricebook XML via WebDAV plus the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job. This is Confluence's recommended pattern for Zimmermann's catalogue scale and is the only pattern that can load price data. Source: Confluence 315490342 (Context callout and Section 9) and 312508418. #### Option B: SCAPI Admin API (supplementary) MuleSoft (or a script) calls the SCAPI Products and Inventory Lists Admin APIs per record, authenticated via Account Manager OAuth2. Suited to real-time single-product updates, not bulk load, and it cannot write pricebooks. Useful later for deltas; not the interim unblock. Source: Confluence 315490342 (Sections 4, 6, and 9). #### Option C: Wait for MuleSoft *(Discarded)* Discarded: it leaves the front-end blocked for an unknown period (dependency on SFCC-121) when an interim load is available. Baseline option; no source document. --- ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale ### 4.1 Recommended Option **Option A: File-based import of the `data/core` structure plus `data/sample` sample data.** ### 4.2 Rationale Option A matches the Confluence-recommended pattern for catalogue scale (per "TSD: Catalogue Sync", 315490342 Section 9 and its parent 312508418), is a single repeatable load, and is the only option that also populates price (per 315490342 Section 5: no pricebook write API exists). It unblocks front-end build and test with no code change and is independent of the MuleSoft feed timeline. Option B is retained only as a supplementary, real-time mechanism; Option C blocks the squad. Note: the Confluence recommendation is written for the permanent MuleSoft to SFCC sync. The same load mechanism (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import`) applies here to the interim sample load, so the recommendation carries over; framing it as the interim unblock is this TSD's extension, not a verbatim Confluence recommendation. ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted The interim sample load is throwaway once the permanent AP21-to-MuleSoft-to-SFCC feed is delivering. It depends on sandbox/WebDAV access and someone running the import (a dependency on platform / Victor), and the sample data is not production-representative. **Status (24 Jul):** for dev, this interim load is already in place, one sample product with an AU list price and inventory (confirmed by Victor and verified via local run). The recommendation now applies to broadening the sample set and extending to other sites and tiers, not to a first load. --- ## 5. Technical Implementation ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence 1. Apply the source-controlled structure: `npm run data:import:core` (`sfcc-ci instance:import`) loads the catalogues (`zimmermann-catalog`, `zimmermann--storefront-catalog`) and the empty pricebook and inventory shells. Safe to re-run. 2. Load sample product data: import the filtered sample catalogue from `data/sample/` (manual, for dev and demo). 3. Load sample prices: deliver Pricebook XML via WebDAV and run the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job. IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices`. 4. Complete first-time BM setup: storefront-catalogue assignment per site, pricebook assignment, and a search-index rebuild. 5. Verify: obtain a SLAS guest token and run a `shopper-search` call for a known category. If it returns zero results, rebuild the search index (step 4) and retry. 6. Front-end consumes product, category, and price via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No code change is required.
